testCases.title: Branded website submission creates a WebsiteLeadSubmission and a lead within 5 seconds with no manual step
testCases.preconditions: An active WebsiteLeadSite exists (isActive=true) with a configured siteId, brandTag, and an allowed origin. Request origin matches the site's allowed-origins list.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/public/leads/capture with valid body {siteId, leadType, company/contact name, email, phone, serviceTechCount} from an allowed Origin header.
2. Observe HTTP status and timing.
3. Query the lead list / submission list as an internal lead.intake_manage user.
testCases.testData: siteId=solace-air-01, leadType=dealer_inquiry, contactName='Jane Doe', email='jane@hvacco.com', phone='+1 614 555 0100', serviceTechCount=3, Origin: https://solaceair.com
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 201 returned within 5s. A lead record is created stamped with source_site_id=solace-air-01, source_brand_tag, capture_method=direct_web_form, sourceDetail=site name; no manual step required. Submission is visible to internal staff.

testCases.title: Submission to an inactive or unknown site is rejected
testCases.preconditions: A WebsiteLeadSite with isActive=false exists; another siteId does not exist.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/public/leads/capture with siteId of an inactive site.
2. POST again with a non-existent siteId.
3. Observe responses.
testCases.expectedResult: Both requests are rejected with an error 'Website lead form is not active for this site'. No lead or submission record is created.

testCases.title: Cross-origin submission from a non-allowed origin is forbidden (allowed-origins enforcement)
testCases.preconditions: Active site solace-air-01 has allowed-origins = [https://solaceair.com] only.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/public/leads/capture for siteId=solace-air-01 with Origin header https://evil.example.com.
2. Observe response and headers.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 403 'Origin is not allowed for this website lead form'. Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is cleared/not granted. No lead created.

testCases.title: Public capture endpoint rate-limits abusive submission bursts per IP and per site
testCases.preconditions: Public capture rate limiter configured (websiteLeadCaptureLimiter). Active site with valid origin.
testCases.steps:
1. From a single client IP, POST valid capture requests in a tight loop exceeding the configured window quota.
2. Observe responses once the quota is exceeded.
3. Repeat for the per-site (siteId) limiter.
testCases.testData: N+1 rapid POSTs to /api/v1/public/leads/capture from same IP for siteId=solace-air-01
testCases.expectedResult: After the quota is exhausted, HTTP 429 'Too many website lead form submissions...' with a Retry-After value. Earlier requests within quota succeed (201). OPTIONS preflight is independently rate-limited.

testCases.title: Authorized internal user creates a manual lead with intake source manual_entry
testCases.preconditions: Routing policy is seeded. Actor has lead.intake_manage (e.g., SALES_BD_REP).
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads with required fields (company, contact, email, phone, serviceTechCount/truckCount per active basis).
2. Observe created lead.
testCases.testData: company='Acme HVAC', contact='Bob Lee', email='bob@acme.com', phone='614-555-0123', serviceTechCount=8
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 201. Lead created with capture_method=manual_entry, lead source defaulting to manual, source attribution present, routed by policy, and an audit entry recorded.

testCases.title: Territory Manager and Regional Director are denied manual lead creation (no lead.intake_manage)
testCases.preconditions: RBAC matrix: TERRITORY_MANAGER and REGIONAL_DIRECTOR hold lead.view but NOT lead.intake_manage. FINANCE also lacks intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. Authenticate as TERRITORY_MANAGER; POST /api/v1/leads with a valid body.
2. Repeat as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR.
3. Repeat as FINANCE.
testCases.testData: Valid create-lead body; roles TERRITORY_MANAGER, REGIONAL_DIRECTOR, FINANCE
testCases.expectedResult: Each returns HTTP 403 (authorization error) — default-deny on lead.intake_manage. No lead is created for any of the three roles.

testCases.title: Invalid email format is rejected at intake across paths
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage. EMAIL_PATTERN /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ enforced server-side.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads with email='notanemail'.
2. POST with email='a@b' (no TLD dot).
3. POST with email='has space@x.com'.
4. Observe each response.
testCases.expectedResult: All rejected with an explicit email validation error at submission; no lead created. (Same rejection applies on website capture path.)

testCases.title: Invalid phone format and out-of-range digit counts are rejected
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage. Phone rule: 7-15 digits, only chars in [\d\s+().-].
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads with phone='123' (6 digits, too short).
2. POST with phone='+1 (614) 555-0123 ext 999 0000 0000' (>15 digits).
3. POST with phone='614-555-ABCD' (illegal chars).
4. Observe responses.
testCases.expectedResult: Each rejected with an explicit phone validation error; no lead created. A valid boundary phone of exactly 7 and exactly 15 digits is accepted.

testCases.title: Lead missing required fields cannot be committed
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads omitting required company/contact identity field.
2. POST omitting the routing metric required by the active basis (serviceTechCount).
3. Observe responses.
testCases.testData: Body with blank companyName; body without serviceTechCount under SERVICE_TECH_COUNT basis
testCases.expectedResult: Missing required identity field is rejected with a required-field error. Missing routing metric is rejected with 'serviceTechCount is required for the active routing policy'. No lead created.

testCases.title: Source attribution (brand tag, site id, capture method, private label) persists through stage changes
testCases.preconditions: Lead created via website capture from solace-air-01 with brandTag set.
testCases.steps:
1. Capture a lead via the branded site.
2. Read lead detail; confirm source_brand_tag, source_site_id, capture_method, private_label_name.
3. Transition the lead through several stages.
4. Re-read detail and confirm attribution unchanged.
testCases.expectedResult: source_brand_tag, source_site_id, capture_method, and private_label_name are stored and remain identical after stage transitions — attribution is retained for per-website reporting (BR-L-13).

testCases.title: Manual create with a matching existing lead is blocked until a duplicate-resolution decision is supplied
testCases.preconditions: An existing lead with email='dupe@acme.com' already exists. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads with the same email/phone as the existing lead and NO duplicateResolution.
2. Observe rejection.
3. POST /api/v1/leads/duplicates/preview to surface candidates.
4. Re-POST with duplicateResolution.decision set.
testCases.expectedResult: Step 1 is rejected: 'Potential duplicate found. Review existing...before creating a new manual lead.' Preview returns hasPotentialDuplicate=true with candidates. With a valid decision, the create proceeds (new, enrich_existing, etc.) and the resolution is recorded in audit/source metadata.

testCases.title: duplicateResolution.targetEntityId not matching any surfaced candidate is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Duplicate candidates exist for the submitted identity. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads with duplicateResolution.targetEntityId set to a random/unrelated id.
2. Observe response.
testCases.expectedResult: Rejected: 'duplicateResolution.targetEntityId must match one of the duplicate candidates'. No lead created.

testCases.title: Repeat website submission attaches to existing lead and preserves submission history
testCases.preconditions: A prior lead exists from the same site/email. Active site, allowed origin.
testCases.steps:
1. POST a website capture matching an existing lead's identity.
2. Inspect the submission outcome and the linked lead's submission history.
testCases.testData: Same email/company as an existing website-sourced lead
testCases.expectedResult: Submission outcome = ATTACHED_TO_EXISTING_LEAD; no new lead created; prior submission history is preserved on the existing lead (no silent duplicate).

testCases.title: Resolving an already-resolved or non-duplicate website submission is rejected
testCases.preconditions: A website submission already resolved (e.g., CONFIRMED_EXISTING); another that is not a repeat/duplicate.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /resolve on a submission that is not a repeat duplicate.
2. POST /resolve a second time on an already-resolved submission with a conflicting decision.
3. POST relink_existing without targetLeadId.
testCases.testData: decision='confirm_existing' on a fresh single submission; second resolve; relink without targetLeadId
testCases.expectedResult: Non-repeat resolve rejected ('Only repeat website submissions require duplicate-resolution actions'); re-resolve rejected ('already been resolved'); relink without target rejected ('targetLeadId is required when relinking').

testCases.title: CSV/XLSX import preview shows mapped rows, flags duplicates and validation errors before commit
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage. A roster file with valid, duplicate, and invalid rows is prepared.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/import/preview (or /import/file) with column mapping.
2. Review the preview run: mapped values, POTENTIAL_DUPLICATE and validation-error flags.
3. POST /import/review with per-row decisions.
4. POST /import/runs/:runId/commit.
testCases.testData: 100-row CSV: 80 valid, 10 dup emails of existing leads, 10 invalid emails
testCases.expectedResult: Preview returns a run with per-row status (valid / potential_duplicate / error). Duplicates and invalid rows are flagged before commit. Per-row decisions accepted; commit creates only the resolved rows; run is auditable by runId.

testCases.title: Import request exceeding the 500-row per-request cap is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/import with rows.length = 501.
2. POST again with rows.length = 500.
3. Observe responses.
testCases.expectedResult: 501 rows rejected: 'rows cannot exceed 500 in one request'. Exactly 500 rows is accepted (boundary).

testCases.title: Affinity/ownership roster import preserves source affinity-group label and surfaces duplicates
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage. Roster file (CSV/XLSX) with variable columns including company, contact, email, state.
testCases.steps:
1. Upload a 1,000-row roster and map source columns to CRM lead fields.
2. Confirm the source affinity-group label is captured.
3. Review duplicate matches before commit; commit.
testCases.testData: 1000-row affinity roster, source column 'Group'='Comfort Pros Alliance'
testCases.expectedResult: Mapping succeeds; affinity-group label persisted on created leads; duplicate leads surfaced for review before commit; preview within 30s and commit within 60s (NFR-L-03).

testCases.title: OCR preview extracts candidate fields from a business card / badge for confirmation
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage. OCR processor configured (PULSE_OCR_PROCESSOR_PATH).
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/ocr/preview with mode='business_card' and contentBase64 (or rawExtractionText).
2. Review extracted name/company/email/phone candidates.
3. Confirm/correct and create the lead.
testCases.expectedResult: OCR preview returns candidate name/company/email/phone for review (no auto-create). User can correct before creating. NOTE/known gap: capture_method cannot yet be recorded as business_card/show_badge on the created lead — LEAD_CAPTURE_METHODS lacks an OCR/card-scan value (FR-L-005 Partial, UX-L-007 needs contract+enum+server change).

testCases.title: OCR preview rejects missing image/text and unsupported document type
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/ocr/preview with neither rawExtractionText nor contentBase64.
2. POST with an unsupported document type.
3. Observe responses.
testCases.expectedResult: Missing input rejected: 'Either rawExtractionText or contentBase64 is required...'. Unsupported type rejected: 'Unsupported lead OCR document type'.

testCases.title: Affinity group and ownership group are stored as two independent fields; changing one does not affect the other
testCases.preconditions: Lead exists. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. PATCH the lead to set affinityGroup=A and ownershipGroup=B.
2. PATCH affinityGroup to C; read back.
3. Confirm ownershipGroup unchanged.
testCases.testData: affinity codes A→C; ownership code B
testCases.expectedResult: Both fields persist independently; updating affinity does not mutate ownership (BR-L-03 — not collapsed into one field). Both carry forward downstream.

testCases.title: Independent/none and unknown classification options are accepted; unknown is not the default and is flagged for resolution
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. Create a lead selecting affinity='independent/none'.
2. Create a lead with affinity='unknown'.
3. Inspect default value on a lead created without an explicit selection.
testCases.expectedResult: Independent/none and unknown are all valid selections. Unknown is a permitted review-state, is not the default, and is flagged for resolution before the CIS stage (ASM-L-03).

testCases.title: Lead rating (cold/warm/hot/whale) is captured and editable by authorized users
testCases.preconditions: Lead exists. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. Create a lead with rating='warm'.
2. PATCH rating to 'whale'.
3. Read list and detail views.
testCases.expectedResult: Rating is stored, visible in list and detail, and updatable at any time by an authorized user.

testCases.title: Routing boundary at threshold — verify <= threshold goes to Strategic Growth (code) vs PRD 'fewer than 5'
testCases.preconditions: Routing policy seeded with strategicGrowthMax=5, basis=SERVICE_TECH_COUNT.
testCases.steps:
1. Create a lead with serviceTechCount=4.
2. Create a lead with serviceTechCount=5.
3. Create a lead with serviceTechCount=6.
4. Inspect routingTeam on each.
testCases.expectedResult: 4 → strategic_growth; 6 → national_tm. BOUNDARY DEFECT WATCH: code uses metricValue <= threshold so 5 → strategic_growth, but PRD FR-L-013 states '5 or more → national_tm'. Confirm intended behavior; flag the off-by-one between PRD and resolveRoutingDecision.

testCases.title: Same routing backbone applied to website, manual, import, and mobile intake
testCases.preconditions: Routing policy seeded (threshold=5).
testCases.steps:
1. Create a sub-threshold lead via each intake path (website capture, manual, import, OCR-confirmed).
2. Inspect routingTeam on each created lead.
testCases.expectedResult: All four paths route the lead to strategic_growth and record routingTeam + routingThresholdSnapshot on the lead, regardless of intake source (BR-L-06).

testCases.title: Changing the routing threshold/basis re-evaluates routing and is auditable
testCases.preconditions: Actor authorized for routing policy update. Existing leads at various tech counts.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/leads/routing-policy.
2. PATCH the policy to threshold=10 (or basis=TRUCK_COUNT).
3. Update a lead's tech count and observe routingTeam recompute + routingThresholdSnapshot change.
4. Inspect audit trail.
testCases.expectedResult: Policy update succeeds. Subsequent lead metric updates recompute routingTeam using the new threshold; routingThresholdSnapshot updates; routing change logged with actor/timestamp/before-after (FR-L-015, NFR-L-08).

testCases.title: Manual reassignment records new owner + reason and preserves prior activity authorship
testCases.preconditions: Lead with existing activity entries authored by user A. Actor authorized for territory.reassign.
testCases.steps:
1. Reassign the lead to a new territory/owner with a reason and note.
2. Inspect ownership history and existing activity entries.
testCases.testData: reason='Moved to West territory', note='per RD request'
testCases.expectedResult: New owner and reason recorded; prior activity entries retain original author A; ownership history is viewable (BR-L-10). Reassignment is in the audit trail.

testCases.title: Territory Manager sees only leads in their own book (server-side scope)
testCases.preconditions: Leads exist in TM-X's territory and in another territory. resolveLeadRecordScope enforced server-side.
testCases.steps:
1. Authenticate as TM-X (assignedTmUserId or territory.managerUserId = TM-X).
2. GET /api/v1/leads.
3. Inspect returned leads and total count.
testCases.testData: TM-X owns 12 leads; 40 other leads exist in other territories
testCases.expectedResult: Only the 12 in-scope leads (plus any preHandoff/manual-override per territoryPolicy) are returned. Out-of-territory leads are excluded by the scope WHERE clause, not the client.

testCases.title: TM cannot read an out-of-scope lead by direct ID (IDOR returns not-found)
testCases.preconditions: Lead L-OTHER belongs to a different territory than TM-X.
testCases.steps:
1. Authenticate as TM-X.
2. GET /api/v1/leads/L-OTHER directly by id.
3. Attempt GET /api/v1/leads/L-OTHER/readiness and history-feed for the same id.
testCases.expectedResult: Detail returns null/404 (scope AND clause prevents access); readiness/history likewise exclude the out-of-scope lead. No data leakage via direct id manipulation.

testCases.title: Duplicate-preview and website-submission enumeration are intake-gated, not exposed to scoped roles
testCases.preconditions: previewLeadDuplicateCandidates and listWebsiteLeadSubmissions require lead.intake_manage (probe whole table).
testCases.steps:
1. Authenticate as TERRITORY_MANAGER (lead.view only).
2. POST /api/v1/leads/duplicates/preview.
3. GET /api/v1/leads/website-submissions.
testCases.expectedResult: Both return HTTP 403 — gated on lead.intake_manage so a scoped role cannot enumerate cross-territory candidates/submissions.

testCases.title: Seven-stage pipeline transitions forward and logs each transition with timestamp
testCases.preconditions: Lead at stage 'new'. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/:id/stage-transition through new → discovery_scheduled → discovery_completed → cis_sent → cis_signed → onboarding_completed → customer_active.
2. Inspect stage events and the stage-entered timestamps.
testCases.testData: Sequential toStage values across all seven stages
testCases.expectedResult: All seven stages present and reachable. Each transition creates a LeadStageEvent + AuditEntry with timestamps and sets the corresponding stage-entered timestamp. NOTE: stage enumeration is vendor-proposed pending client field-list review (FR-L-018 correction).

testCases.title: Transition to the same stage and invalid stage key are rejected
testCases.preconditions: Lead at stage 'cis_sent'. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST stage-transition with toStage='cis_sent' (same as current).
2. POST with toStage='banana' (not in LEAD_STAGES).
testCases.expectedResult: Same-stage rejected: 'Lead is already at the requested stage'. Invalid enum value rejected by stage-key conversion. No transition recorded.

testCases.title: Backward stage transition requires a mandatory reason and stores it in the audit trail
testCases.preconditions: Lead at stage 'cis_sent'. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST stage-transition toStage='discovery_completed' (earlier) WITHOUT backwardReason → expect rejection.
2. POST again WITH backwardReason.
3. Inspect stage event + audit metadata.
testCases.expectedResult: Step 1 rejected: 'A reason is required to move a lead to an earlier stage (BR-L-07).' Step 2 succeeds; isBackwardTransition=true and backwardReason stored in both the stage event and AuditEntry.

testCases.title: Out-of-order forward progression (CIS before discovery) is permitted with incomplete earlier steps shown
testCases.preconditions: Lead at stage 'new' (no discovery completed). Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. Transition directly toStage='cis_sent' skipping discovery stages.
2. Inspect lead — earlier discovery step shown incomplete, forward progress not blocked.
testCases.expectedResult: Forward, out-of-order transition succeeds (no backward reason needed). Skipped earlier steps are marked incomplete without blocking progression (Michelle Hogan: steps don't always go in order).

testCases.title: Parking and closing a lead requires a reason; reopen clears reason; CUSTOMER_ACTIVE cannot be parked
testCases.preconditions: Active lead not at CUSTOMER_ACTIVE; a separate lead at stage CUSTOMER_ACTIVE. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. PATCH lifecycle to 'parked' WITHOUT reasonCode → expect rejection.
2. PATCH to 'parked' with reasonCode='follow_up_later'.
3. PATCH back to 'active' (reopen).
4. On the CUSTOMER_ACTIVE lead, PATCH to 'closed'.
testCases.expectedResult: Park/close without reason rejected ('A lifecycle reason is required...'). Park with reason succeeds and is auditable. Reopen sets active and nulls reason. Parking/closing a CUSTOMER_ACTIVE lead rejected ('Customer Active records cannot be parked or closed from the lead lifecycle'). KNOWN UI GAP: lifecycle badge missing on list rows (UX-L-004).

testCases.title: Time-in-stage tracked; stagnant leads surface in the workflow queue
testCases.preconditions: A lead whose stage-entered timestamp exceeds policy.stagnantStageDays.
testCases.steps:
1. Backdate a lead's stage-entered timestamp past the stagnant threshold.
2. GET /api/v1/leads/workflow-queue (urgent/stagnant view).
testCases.testData: stagnantStageDays=14; lead in stage for 20 days
testCases.expectedResult: Lead appears in the Urgent/Stagnant workflow queue with computed time-in-stage; non-stagnant leads do not appear.

testCases.title: Schedule discovery only allowed from the New Lead stage; surfaces on calendar
testCases.preconditions: Lead at stage 'new'; another lead at 'cis_sent'. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/:id/discovery/schedule on the new-stage lead.
2. Attempt the same on the cis_sent-stage lead.
3. Verify the calendar event link.
testCases.expectedResult: New-stage scheduling succeeds and creates a calendar-linked event (UX-L-016). Scheduling from a non-new stage is rejected: 'Discovery can only be scheduled while the lead is in the New Lead stage'. (Calendar wiring is partial per FR-L-023.)

testCases.title: Logging initial contact stops the SLA timer; double-logging is rejected
testCases.preconditions: New lead with no initial contact logged. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/:id/log-initial-contact.
2. Inspect first-contact timestamp and SLA state.
3. POST log-initial-contact again.
testCases.expectedResult: First call records firstContact timestamp and SLA state reflects within/over window. Second call rejected: 'Initial contact has already been logged for this lead.'

testCases.title: Completing discovery captures structured outcomes and advances stage; re-completion blocked
testCases.preconditions: Lead with discovery open. Actor has lead.intake_manage and (for consignment fields) consignment access.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/:id/discovery/complete with summary, painPoints, decisionMaker, buyingIntent, consignmentInterestStatus.
2. Confirm lead advances to discovery_completed.
3. POST complete again.
testCases.expectedResult: Discovery outcomes (summary, pain points, decision maker, buying intent, consignment interest+timing) persist; lead moves to discovery_completed; audit + consignment capture recorded. Re-completion rejected: 'Discovery is already closed for this lead.'

testCases.title: Skipping discovery with an approved reason advances toward CIS and stores the reason
testCases.preconditions: Lead with discovery open. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/:id/discovery/skip with a skip reason.
2. Inspect audit trail and stage progression.
3. Attempt skip again on an already-closed discovery.
testCases.expectedResult: Skip records the reason in the audit trail and allows advance toward cis_sent without a formal discovery. Re-skip after discovery closed is rejected.

testCases.title: CIS lifecycle state (not_sent → sent → received/incomplete → signed) is visible and logged
testCases.preconditions: Qualified lead handed into CIS path. Actor authorized.
testCases.steps:
1. Open the CIS panel for the lead.
2. Move CIS state through sent, received, signed.
3. Inspect status timestamps and audit.
testCases.expectedResult: CIS state is visible on the lead at all times; each change is logged with a timestamp; panel reachable from the lead record.

testCases.title: Finance decision queue and decisioning is restricted to finance roles (RBAC)
testCases.preconditions: lead.finance_queue_view held by FINANCE & SALES_BD_LEADERSHIP; lead.finance_decide held by FINANCE only. A lead awaiting credit decision exists.
testCases.steps:
1. As FINANCE, view finance queue and update decision status to approved.
2. As SALES_BD_REP (no finance perms), attempt to view the finance queue and update a decision.
3. As SALES_BD_LEADERSHIP, attempt to decide (queue view only).
testCases.expectedResult: FINANCE can view and decide. SALES_BD_REP is 403 on both queue view and decide. SALES_BD_LEADERSHIP can view the queue but is 403 on lead.finance_decide (default-deny on the missing action).

testCases.title: Importing contacts from a received CIS populates lead contact fields without re-entry
testCases.preconditions: Lead with a received CIS containing contact data. Actor has lead.intake_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/:id/contacts/import-from-cis.
2. Inspect lead contacts.
testCases.expectedResult: Contact fields are auto-populated from CIS data; new lead contacts appear without manual re-entry.

testCases.title: No raw credit-card number is persisted via CIS/lead flow (PCI hard requirement)
testCases.preconditions: PARKED dependency: PCI-compliant tokenization provider not integrated. CIS card-on-file capture descoped/deferred per client (Apr 20).
testCases.steps:
1. Inspect the CIS/lead schema and intake forms for any raw card-number field.
2. Attempt to submit a payload containing a 16-digit card number in a free-text/notes field.
3. Inspect DB, logs, and file store for the card number.
testCases.testData: Card number '4111 1111 1111 1111' submitted in available fields
testCases.expectedResult: No DB column accepts a raw card number; no card number is persisted in any table, log, or file store. KNOWN GAP: explicit card-input rejection is not yet enforced in the CIS form (OQ-L-01 open) — test should assert no storage and flag the missing explicit block. Tokenization provider integration is parked.

testCases.title: Conversion is blocked when critical readiness items are incomplete
testCases.preconditions: Lead with an incomplete readiness checklist (e.g., finance not approved). Actor has customer.create and lead scope.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/leads/:id/conversion-prep/validate (or readiness blockers).
2. POST /api/v1/leads/:id/convert-on-first-order with firstOrderConfirmedAt.
testCases.expectedResult: Validation reports blockers; conversion is rejected: 'Lead is not ready for conversion: <blockers>'. No account is created.

testCases.title: Lead converts to a customer/account only on confirmed first order; classification/territory carry forward; Acumatica sync parked
testCases.preconditions: Lead with readiness=ready. Actor has customers module + customer.create and the lead is in actor's scope. Acumatica endpoint PARKED.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/leads/:id/convert-on-first-order with firstOrderConfirmedAt.
2. Inspect created account: affinity/ownership/territory/contacts carried forward.
3. Confirm lead remains as historical evidence; ownership transfer to TM recorded.
testCases.expectedResult: Account created from lead backbone with affinity, ownership, territory, TM/RD assignment, contacts and addresses carried forward; lifecycle reflects converted; CIS alone does not convert (BR-L-01). Acumatica push is NOT attempted (parked, ASM-L-08). TM notification delivery pending Graph (FR-L-035 Partial).

testCases.title: TM cannot convert an out-of-scope lead despite holding customer.create
testCases.preconditions: TERRITORY_MANAGER holds customer.create but the target lead is in another territory.
testCases.steps:
1. Authenticate as TM-X.
2. POST /api/v1/leads/L-OTHER/convert-on-first-order.
testCases.expectedResult: Conversion rejected with 'Lead not found' — convertLeadOnFirstOrder gates on isLeadVisibleToActor so a scoped role cannot convert any system-wide ready lead.

testCases.title: Re-converting an already-converted lead and converting without first-order date are rejected

testCases.title: Freeform note logging records type, author, timestamp; empty note rejected

testCases.title: Stage/lifecycle/routing/field changes each produce an immutable audit entry with before/after and actor

testCases.title: Voice-to-text note entry in the mobile app (not yet built)

testCases.title: Operational alerts (assigned, SLA breach, discovery overdue, CIS follow-up) are persisted with dedup key; email delivery parked

testCases.title: Quiet-hours configuration defers alert delivery to the next available window

testCases.expectedResult: Alert is queued during quiet hours and scheduled for delivery at the next available window rather than sent immediately.

testCases.title: SLA breach is surfaced on the lead (hero banner gap) and in the workflow queue

testCases.title: Lead list uses server-side pagination; per-page limit clamps to 200 and defaults to 50

testCases.expectedResult: Default page size = 50. limit is clamped to max 200 (limit=500 returns ≤200); limit ≤0 clamps to min 1. Pagination via page offset returns distinct pages — no hard 200-row total cap on the dataset (UX-L-013 done).

testCases.title: Filter by affinity group, ownership group, source, stage, lifecycle, territory, routing team
testCases.preconditions: Leads exist across multiple groups/sources/stages. Actor has lead.view.
testCases.steps:

3. Verify results match all filters and respect record scope.
testCases.expectedResult: Group code filters use UPPER_SNAKE normalization (normalizeGroupCode) and match correctly; all filter dimensions narrow the list/Kanban consistently and remain within the actor's record scope.

testCases.title: List and Kanban views render seven stage columns; empty-state prompts (UI gap)

testCases.title: Insights computed server-side: time-in-stage, SLA breach trend, pipeline value, territory breakdown

testCases.expectedResult: Insights metrics are present and computed server-side over the full dataset (UX-L-012 done), not from a client-side 200-row sample.

testCases.title: Admin configures a website form, previews it, and runs a test submission without creating a production lead

testCases.title: Injection and unicode/special-character payloads are stored/escaped safely, not executed
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage. Parameterized Prisma queries in use.
testCases.steps:

testCases.title: Concurrent identical lead creates do not produce silent duplicates (transactional duplicate guard)
testCases.preconditions: No existing lead for the identity. Two authorized intake users submit simultaneously.
testCases.steps:

2. Observe outcomes.
testCases.testData: Same email='race@acme.com' from two parallel requests
testCases.expectedResult: The transactional duplicate check (findLeadImportDuplicateCandidates within $transaction) plus DB unique constraint (P2002) prevents two silently-created duplicates; at most one lead is created and the second is blocked/flagged for resolution rather than silently duplicated.

testCases.title: Email at max length boundary (254) and over-length are handled correctly
testCases.preconditions: Actor has lead.intake_manage. EMAIL max length = 254.
testCases.steps:

testCases.expectedResult: 254-char email accepted; 255-char email rejected as invalid (length > 254). No lead created for the over-length case.

testCases.title: Truck/service-tech count rejects negatives and non-integers; zero is handled per policy

testCases.expectedResult: Negative and non-integer values rejected by positive-integer normalization. Zero (if accepted) routes to strategic_growth (0 <= 5). No lead created for invalid values.

testCases.title: Unauthenticated request to any internal lead endpoint is rejected

testCases.expectedResult: All return HTTP 401 (authentication error) before any business logic runs. Only the public capture endpoints (/api/v1/public/...) are unauthenticated by design.

testCases.title: Consignment interest status and entry timing persist on the lead and carry through conversion

testCases.title: Training Ops creates a training category with all attributes
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated as TRAINING_OPS (holds training.catalog_manage). Training catalog seeded.

testCases.expectedResult: 201 Created; category persisted with the supplied kind/code/name/sortOrder/active flag; appears in catalog list; an AuditEntry (action=CREATE, entityType training category) is written.

testCases.title: Seeded default categories/types/templates load automatically on first catalog use
testCases.preconditions: Fresh environment (no manual catalog creation). Authenticated as any training-module role.

testCases.expectedResult: Default categories load automatically (ONBOARDING, PRODUCT, TECHNICAL, SALES, COMPLIANCE, CERTIFICATION, CUSTOM, VISIT kinds present); each type has at least one default template; no manual seeding required.

testCases.title: Deactivated category remains visible on prior sessions

testCases.testData: Existing category code with historical session linkage
testCases.expectedResult: Category is no longer selectable for new scheduling but its name/kind still renders on prior sessions and history (retired categories remain visible on prior records).

testCases.title: Non-catalog roles are denied creating a category (default-deny)

testCases.title: Category creation rejects missing code/name

testCases.expectedResult: 400 Bad Request with message 'code and name are required'; no record created.

testCases.title: Create training type with delivery mode, duration and certification flags

testCases.testData: { categoryCode:'TECH', code:'INSTALL-101', title:'Install Basics', deliveryMode:'ON_SITE', defaultDurationMinutes:60, isCertificationTrack:false, countsTowardHours:true }

testCases.title: Training type rejects zero/negative default duration

testCases.title: Certification-track type defaults template to CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED; visit type to NOTES_ONLY

testCases.title: Cadence policy drives overdue logic; onboarding defaults 30d, ongoing 180d

testCases.title: Trainers endpoint returns only eligible active roles

testCases.title: Stale Outlook availability warning shown but does not block scheduling

testCases.title: A session cannot exist without an account and is queryable by account

testCases.title: TM cannot create/read training against an account outside their book

testCases.title: Creating an account training program calculates nextDueAt from cadence

testCases.expectedResult: 201 Created; program status ACTIVE; nextDueAt = now + cadenceDays; appears in account history; AuditEntry CREATE written with actor, entityType program.

testCases.title: Program creation rejects unknown type/template and cross-type template

testCases.expectedResult: 400 with 'Training type not found' / 'Training template not found' / 'Training template does not belong to the selected training type' respectively; no program created.

testCases.title: Onboarding program can be initiated on customer activation (first order)

testCases.title: Account history distinguishes onboarding from ongoing programs

testCases.expectedResult: History shows each program's category kind; onboarding programs clearly labelled; ops queue/sessions filterable by program type.

testCases.title: TM coaching workload shows only own-book obligations with overdue KPI

testCases.title: Reject past scheduledAt and non-positive duration

testCases.title: Reject session with program/location not belonging to the account

testCases.title: Centralized calendar shows scheduled sessions with week/month/list and type filter

testCases.title: Only SCHEDULED sessions can be rescheduled

testCases.title: Complete session with checkout notes and attendance

testCases.preconditions: A visible session. Authenticated with training.schedule.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/training/sessions/{id}/follow-up-tasks with owner, dueDate, description.
2. POST /api/v1/training/follow-up-tasks/{taskId}/complete.
3. Re-complete the same task.
testCases.testData: { ownerUserId, dueDate: now+7d, description: 'Send install guide' }
testCases.expectedResult: 201 task OPEN; complete -> 200 COMPLETED with completedAt; open follow-up count reflected in coaching KPI; second complete -> 400 'Only open follow-up tasks can be completed'.

testCases.title: Cancel and no-show only from SCHEDULED; invalid target status rejected
testCases.preconditions: A SCHEDULED visible session and a COMPLETED session.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/training/sessions/{scheduledId}/cancel with status=cancelled and a reason note.
2. POST cancel with status=completed (invalid terminal).
3. POST cancel on the COMPLETED session.
testCases.expectedResult: Valid cancel -> 200 CANCELLED (reason stored in notes; AuditEntry written); invalid status -> 400 'Unsupported training session terminal status'; from COMPLETED -> 400 'Only scheduled training sessions can be cancelled or marked no-show'. No-show path behaves equivalently.

testCases.title: Cancel/no-show accepted with no reason despite PRD 'required reason'
testCases.preconditions: A SCHEDULED visible session. Authenticated with training.schedule.
testCases.steps:
1. POST cancel with status=no_show and no notes/reason field.
2. Inspect persisted record.
testCases.expectedResult: Server currently transitions to NO_SHOW WITHOUT enforcing a required reason (reason is stored as optional notes only). Documents a divergence from FR-TRN-034 'required reason' — flag for product/engineering review; UI should enforce reason capture.

testCases.feature: Proof — Upload happy path & type/size limits
testCases.title: Upload proof PDF/JPEG within 4 MB; reject disallowed type and oversize
testCases.preconditions: Proof storage configured. A non-terminal visible session. Authenticated with training.schedule.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/training/sessions/{id}/proof with a valid JPEG ~1 MB.
2. POST with an EXE/zip mimeType.
3. POST with a file whose decoded size > 4 MB.
4. POST with empty fileName / missing mimeType.
testCases.expectedResult: Valid -> 201, document PENDING review, proofAttachmentCount incremented, AuditEntry. Disallowed -> 400 'Unsupported training proof file type'. Oversize -> 400 'Training proof file cannot exceed 4 MB'. Missing fields -> 400 'fileName is required'/'mimeType is required'.

testCases.title: Proof upload request body capped at 8 MB at API boundary
testCases.preconditions: Proof storage configured. Visible session. Authenticated with training.schedule.
testCases.steps: 1. POST proof with a JSON body exceeding 8 MB (e.g. ~9 MB base64).
testCases.expectedResult: Request rejected by the 8 MB body limit before/at parsing (readJsonBody TRAINING_PROOF_UPLOAD_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES); upload not stored.

testCases.title: Proof cannot be uploaded to cancelled or no-show sessions
testCases.preconditions: A CANCELLED and a NO_SHOW visible session. Storage configured.
testCases.steps:
1. POST proof to the CANCELLED session.
2. POST proof to the NO_SHOW session.
testCases.expectedResult: 400 'Proof cannot be uploaded to cancelled or no-show sessions' in both cases; no document created.

testCases.title: Review sets status/reviewer; download verifies checksum
testCases.preconditions: An uploaded PENDING proof document on a visible session. Storage configured.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/training/proof-documents/{docId}/review with reviewStatus=APPROVED.
2. GET /api/v1/training/proof-documents/{docId}/download.
3. Simulate stored-object checksum mismatch and re-download.
testCases.expectedResult: Review -> 200 with reviewer + APPROVED + AuditEntry. Download -> 200 with content/sha256. On mismatch -> 400 'Training proof document checksum mismatch'.

testCases.title: TM cannot review/download proof on an out-of-scope session's document
testCases.preconditions: Proof document on a session belonging to another TM's book. Authenticated as TM-1.
testCases.steps:
1. As TM-1, POST review on the foreign document id.
2. As TM-1, GET download on the foreign document id.
testCases.expectedResult: 404 'Training proof document not found' (session scope applied to the document lookup); no review/download leakage across books.

testCases.title: Sessions list shows a proof-required badge before execution
testCases.preconditions: Sessions list open with sessions of CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED and NOTES_ONLY templates.
testCases.steps:
1. Open the sessions list in TrainingWorkspace.
2. Look for a proof-required badge column.
testCases.expectedResult: A 'proof required' badge indicates scheduled sessions with an unfulfilled proof obligation. Currently NOT built (UX-T-003 Open) — test expected to fail until the badge column is implemented.

testCases.feature: Retention — No delete of completed records
testCases.title: No delete endpoint exists for completed sessions or proof documents
testCases.preconditions: A COMPLETED session with proof documents.
testCases.steps:
1. Attempt DELETE on /api/v1/training/sessions/{id} and proof-documents/{id}.
2. Review available training routes.
testCases.expectedResult: 405/404 — no DELETE route is wired for sessions or proof documents; completed records and proofs are retained (S3 persistent keys); retention enforced at storage layer.

testCases.title: Completing a cert-track session with AWARDED issues an ACTIVE certification
testCases.preconditions: A SCHEDULED session whose type isCertificationTrack=true (e.g. iaq_certification_curriculum). Authenticated with training.schedule.
testCases.steps:
1. POST complete with checkoutNotes and certificationOutcome=AWARDED (+ optional title/code/expiresAt).
2. Inspect created certification record and account cert history.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 COMPLETED; TrainingCertificationRecord created status ACTIVE, awardedAt=checkedOutAt, awardedByUser=completing actor; record visible on account history; CREATE AuditEntry written.

testCases.title: Resolve a PENDING_DECISION cert session to AWARDED / NOT_AWARDED
testCases.preconditions: A COMPLETED cert-track session with certificationOutcome=PENDING_DECISION (in ops-queue pendingCertificationDecisionCount). Authenticated with training.schedule.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/training/sessions/{id}/certification-decision with certificationOutcome=awarded.
2. Repeat scenario with not_awarded on a second pending session.
testCases.expectedResult: Awarded -> 200, certification record ACTIVE created + audit; not_awarded -> 200, no certification record created; both decisions audit-logged; session removed from pending-decision queue.

testCases.title: Certification-decision rejected for wrong state/type/outcome
testCases.preconditions: Sessions in various states: SCHEDULED cert-track; COMPLETED non-cert-track; COMPLETED cert-track already AWARDED.
testCases.steps:
1. POST decision on the SCHEDULED cert session.
2. POST decision on the COMPLETED non-cert session.
3. POST decision on a session whose outcome is already AWARDED.
4. POST decision with certificationOutcome='maybe'.
testCases.expectedResult: 400 'Only completed training sessions can resolve certification decisions' / 'Certification decisions can only be resolved for certification-track sessions' / 'Only pending certification decisions can be resolved' / 'certificationOutcome must be awarded or not_awarded' respectively.

testCases.title: Revoke an active certification with a reason; idempotent on re-revoke
testCases.preconditions: An ACTIVE certification visible to actor. Authenticated with training.schedule.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/training/certifications/{certId}/revoke with notes reason.
2. POST revoke again on the same certification.
testCases.expectedResult: First call -> 200 status REVOKED, reason appended to lifecycle notes, UPDATE AuditEntry written. Second call -> 200 returns existing REVOKED record (idempotent, no duplicate audit/state churn).

testCases.title: Revocation has no confirmation step before submission
testCases.preconditions: TrainingCertificationOpsModal open on an ACTIVE certification.
testCases.steps:
1. Trigger revoke in the modal.
2. Observe whether a confirmation prompt precedes submission.
testCases.expectedResult: Per FR-TRN-053 revocation should require a confirmation step; currently NO confirmation step exists (UX-T-001 Open) — server still revokes. Flagged as a UX gap; test expected to fail until confirmation added.

testCases.title: Recertification queue lists expiring/expired certs scoped to actor
testCases.preconditions: Certs expiring within window across TM-1 and TM-2 books. Authenticated as TM-1.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/training/recertification?windowDays=30 as TM-1.
2. Inspect items (account, cert type, expiry date, days-until-expiry) and confirm TM-2 certs excluded.
testCases.expectedResult: Queue returns expiring/expired certs scoped to TM-1; items include account, type, expiry, days-to-expiry; TM-2 certs excluded. API built; rendering/scheduled-renewal CTA is UX-T-004 Open.

testCases.title: Certification completion records gift-card/demo-unit reward association
testCases.preconditions: A cert-track completion (IAQ -> demo unit; Product Installations -> $50 gift card).
testCases.steps:
1. Complete a Product Installations certification.
2. Attempt to record/view a linked reward (program/giveaway) on the certification.
testCases.testData: Product Installations cert; $50 gift card reward
testCases.expectedResult: Reward linkage to the program/giveaway module is NOT built (FR-TRN-055 Not built; vendor-proposed/deferred pending OQ-TRN-008). No reward association is persisted; tracked outside Pulse for now.

testCases.title: RD sees all territory programs in region; TM does not see other regions
testCases.preconditions: RD-1 over Region-A (multiple territories); TM in Region-B. Data across both regions.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/training/coaching and /territory-penetration as RD-1.
2. Confirm Region-B data absent.
3. Attempt drill-through from a coaching row to the account program.
testCases.expectedResult: RD-1 receives all Region-A territory programs with per-territory/per-region breakdowns; Region-B excluded. Drill-through from coaching row to account program is UX-T-002 Open (not wired) — drill-through step expected to fail.

testCases.title: Territory penetration report returns coverage, hours, overdue, active certs
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated as RD/leadership with multiple territories of data.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/training/territory-penetration.
2. Inspect per-territory and per-region summaries; open the reports tab table.
testCases.expectedResult: Returns per-territory and per-region coverage %, hours delivered, overdue count, active certifications. Penetration table now present in reports tab (UX-T-009 marked Done).

testCases.title: Training hours from actual duration; compliance report rollups exportable
testCases.preconditions: Completed sessions across accounts/trainers/periods. Authenticated as training-module role.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/training/overview (deliveredTrainingHours).
2. GET /api/v1/training/reporting and inspect per-account, per-owner, cert-track and hours rollups.
testCases.testData: Sessions with varying durationMinutes; countsTowardHours true/false types
testCases.expectedResult: deliveredTrainingHours = sum of completed training-activity sessions where type countsTowardHours; compliance report returns all rollup types and is surfaced for leadership review (month + YTD intent).

testCases.title: Ops queue surfaces overdue, exceptions and pending cert decisions with filters
testCases.preconditions: Overdue programs, execution exceptions and pending cert sessions exist. Authenticated as TRAINING_OPS.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/training/ops.
2. GET /api/v1/training/ops?ownerTmUserId={tm}&limit=5.
3. Pass a non-integer limit/certificationWindowDays.
testCases.expectedResult: Returns cadence-overdue, execution-exception and pending-certification items in one prioritized view; owner/limit filters apply; non-integer query params are ignored (parseInteger returns undefined) rather than erroring.

testCases.title: Roles without training module access are denied all read endpoints
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated as a role lacking the training module (e.g. SALES_REP / dealer-portal user).
testCases.steps: 1. GET /api/v1/training/overview, /coaching, /sessions, /accounts as the non-training role.
testCases.expectedResult: 403 Forbidden on each (assertModuleAccess 'training' default-deny). Training module read is limited to TERRITORY_MANAGER, REGIONAL_DIRECTOR, TRAINING_OPS and global-visibility/admin/leadership roles.

testCases.title: Unauthenticated requests are rejected on all training routes
testCases.preconditions: No/invalid bearer token.
testCases.steps:
1. Call a GET (overview) and a POST (sessions) training route with no token.
2. Repeat with an expired/garbage token.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized on every training endpoint; no data returned or mutated (requireAuthenticatedActor / isAuthenticationError path).

testCases.title: Special-character / unicode / SQL-ish payloads handled safely in text fields
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated with training.schedule; visible session/account.
testCases.steps:
1. Create a program/session with title/notes containing SQL meta and unicode (e.g. "'; DROP TABLE--" and emoji 😀).
2. Complete a session with checkoutNotes containing script tags.
3. Read back via API and UI.
testCases.expectedResult: Inputs stored as inert text via parameterized Prisma queries (no SQL execution); values round-trip safely; rendered escaped in UI (no XSS). No injection or data corruption.

testCases.title: Every mutating training operation writes an AuditEntry with before/after
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated actor; visible records for create/complete/cancel/cert-decision/revoke.
testCases.steps:
1. Perform: create category, create program, create+complete session, cancel session, resolve cert decision, revoke cert, upload proof.
2. Query AuditEntry for each entity.
testCases.expectedResult: Each operation produces an AuditEntry with actorUserId, action, entityType, entityId and before/after (and operation metadata where applicable); read-only endpoints write none.

testCases.title: Sessions list and coaching view load within 3 seconds
testCases.preconditions: Representative data volume (hundreds of sessions/programs). Standard web connection.
testCases.steps:
1. Load the sessions list view and measure time to interactive.
2. Load the coaching workload view and measure.
testCases.expectedResult: Both views render within 3 seconds on a standard connection; large lists respect the configurable limit (pagination) without timeout.

testCases.title: Full session lifecycle executable from mobile incl. camera proof
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated TM on a mobile-appropriate surface; visible session.
testCases.steps: 1. On mobile, schedule, check-in, complete (notes + attendee count), and upload a camera photo as proof.
testCases.expectedResult: All lifecycle operations succeed via the API used by the mobile surface; execution modal is mobile-appropriate; proof upload accepts camera JPEG/PNG. API built; dedicated mobile surface not separately confirmed.

testCases.title: Offline session completion queues locally and syncs on reconnect
testCases.preconditions: Field device offline; training-specific offline queue not yet wired (parked).
testCases.steps:
1. Complete a session with no connectivity.
2. Restore connectivity and observe sync.
testCases.expectedResult: Intended: data queues locally and syncs to the server on reconnect (mirroring consignment mobile-draft-queue). Currently PARKED — training offline queue design not confirmed/wired (OQ-TRN-010 pending). Test deferred until implemented.

testCases.title: Voice-to-text available on the notes field during execution
testCases.preconditions: Mobile execution modal open on the notes field.
testCases.steps: 1. Attempt voice-to-text dictation into the notes field.
testCases.expectedResult: Voice-to-text input is NOT built (FR-TRN-072 Not built; confirmed future capability). Test deferred until the capability ships.

testCases.title: Authorized admin creates a region with director and active flag
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR or SUPER_ADMIN (holds territory.admin). A valid active INTERNAL user exists to act as director.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/regions with a code, name, directorUserId and isActive=true.
2. Inspect the 201 response body.
3. GET /api/v1/territories/regions and confirm the region is listed.
4. Query the audit log for the region entity.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 201; region persisted with code normalized to snake_case (southeast_region), directorUser FK set, isActive=true; region appears in GET list; an AuditEntry with action=CREATE and operation 'territory.create_region' is written.

testCases.title: Create region without director (optional FK omitted)
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/regions with code and name only, no directorUserId.
2. Inspect response.
3. GET /api/v1/territories/dashboard and inspect queue summary.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 201; region created with directorUserId=null; dashboard queue 'regionsMissingDirector' count includes this region as a hygiene item (NFR-TR-007 safe degradation).

testCases.title: Territory Manager cannot create a region (territory.admin default-deny)
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as TERRITORY_MANAGER (has territories module access but NOT territory.admin).
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/regions with a valid body.
2. Inspect the response status and body.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 403 Forbidden (AuthorizationError from assertActionAccess); no region created; no CREATE audit entry written.

testCases.title: Executive (read-only oversight) cannot create or edit a region
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as EXECUTIVE (global visibility, no territory.admin after 2026-06-22 hardening).
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/regions with a valid body.
2. PATCH /api/v1/territories/regions/{id} on an existing region.
testCases.expectedResult: Both requests return HTTP 403; EXECUTIVE may read (GET) but cannot mutate any territory record.

testCases.title: Role without territories module access is denied all territory endpoints
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SALES_BD_REP (territories NOT in ROLE_DEFAULT_MODULE_ACCESS). Repeat conceptually for FINANCE, ADMIN_CSR_OPS, TRAINING_OPS, DEALER_PORTAL_USER.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/territories/dashboard.
2. GET /api/v1/territories.
3. GET /api/v1/territories/regions.
testCases.expectedResult: All requests return HTTP 403 (assertModuleAccess('territories') fails) — default-deny enforced for non-territory roles.

testCases.title: Update region director and verify before/after audit
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. An existing region with directorUserId=A and a second active RD user B.
testCases.steps:
1. PATCH /api/v1/territories/regions/{id} setting directorUserId=B.
2. Inspect 200 response.
3. Inspect audit entry beforeData/afterData.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; directorUserId updated to B; AuditEntry UPDATE records beforeData(director=A) and afterData(director=B); lead/account assignments refreshed (reasonCode region_refresh).

testCases.title: Update non-existent region returns 404
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN.
testCases.steps: 1. PATCH /api/v1/territories/regions/non-existent-id with a valid body.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 404 with { error:'NOT_FOUND', detail:'Region not found' }; no mutation or audit entry.

testCases.title: Regional Director cannot update a region outside their scope (404 masking)
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR for Region X. A separate Region Y is directed by another RD.
testCases.steps:
1. PATCH /api/v1/territories/regions/{RegionY id} attempting to change its director.
2. Observe status.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 404 'Region not found' (out-of-scope read masked as not-found by buildRegionReadScope) — RD cannot enumerate or mutate other regions; no audit entry.

testCases.title: Create territory linked to region with manager and shipping center
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. An active region, an active TERRITORY_MANAGER user, and an active shipping center exist.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories with code, name, regionId, managerUserId, shippingCenterId.
2. Inspect 201 response.
3. GET /api/v1/territories and confirm presence.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 201; territory created with FK to region, managerUser and shippingCenter set; coverage attached separately (empty initially); CREATE audit entry written.

testCases.title: Reject territory manager assignment when user role is not TERRITORY_MANAGER
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. A user that is active INTERNAL but with role FINANCE (not TM).
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories with managerUserId pointing to the FINANCE user.
2. Inspect status and message.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 with message 'Selected user must have role TERRITORY_MANAGER' (validateOptionalTerritoryOwnerUserId enforces role match); territory not created.

testCases.title: Reject territory creation referencing an inactive or unknown region
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. A region that has been deactivated (isActive=false).
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories with regionId of the inactive/unknown region.
2. Inspect status and message.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 with message 'Unknown or inactive region' (requireRegion); no territory created.

testCases.title: RD cannot create a territory in a region they do not direct
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR of Region X. Region Y is directed by a different RD.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories with regionId = Region Y.
2. Inspect status and message.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 'Unknown or inaccessible region' (assertRegionInScope blocks out-of-scope region); no territory created.

testCases.title: Update territory: move to a different region the RD controls and refresh assignments
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR directing both Region X and Region Y. A territory in Region X with assigned leads.
testCases.steps:
1. PATCH /api/v1/territories/{id} with regionId=Region Y.
2. Inspect 200.
3. Inspect audit + that downstream lead/account assignments were refreshed.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; territory.regionId updated; UPDATE audit entry; refreshLeadTerritoryAssignments and refreshAccountTerritoryAssignments run (reasonCode territory_refresh) propagating the new RD downstream.

testCases.title: Patch territory with empty name string is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. An existing territory.
testCases.steps:
1. PATCH /api/v1/territories/{id} with name set to whitespace only.
2. Inspect status.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 with message 'name is required' (requireText trims and rejects blank); territory unchanged.

testCases.title: Default NV, FL, NJ shipping centers seeded on first boot
testCases.preconditions: Fresh database; ensureTerritoryPolicySeeded() runs at startup.
testCases.steps:
1. Boot the API / run seeding.
2. GET /api/v1/territories/shipping-centers as SUPER_ADMIN.
3. Inspect returned codes/states.
testCases.expectedResult: Three default shipping centers (NV, FL, NJ) exist and are active; seeding is idempotent (upsert on code) so a second boot does not duplicate them.

testCases.title: Create shipping center normalizes state to a valid US state / Canadian province
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/shipping-centers with a recognizable state name 'Florida'.
2. POST again with an invalid state token 'ZZ'.
3. Compare results.
testCases.testData: Valid: { code:'Tampa Hub', name:'Tampa', state:'Florida', city:'Tampa' }; Invalid: { code:'Bad', name:'Bad', state:'ZZ' }
testCases.expectedResult: Valid request: HTTP 201 with state normalized to 'FL' and countryCode defaulted to 'US'. Invalid 'ZZ': state normalizes to undefined (stored null) since findLeadRegionOption does not resolve it — center is created with null state rather than persisting a bogus code.

testCases.title: Replace territory coverage atomically with new state set
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. A territory with existing coverage [GA].
testCases.steps:
1. PUT /api/v1/territories/{id}/coverage with coverage [FL, SC].
2. Inspect 200 response coverage.
3. Inspect audit before/after.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; prior coverage [GA] deleted and [FL,SC] inserted in a single transaction; AuditEntry UPDATE on TERRITORY_COVERAGE with beforeData coverage=[US:GA] and afterData=[US:FL,US:SC]; lead/account assignments refreshed for both old and new states.

testCases.title: Reject coverage state already owned by a different active territory
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. State FL is already covered by Territory A. Territory B has no FL coverage.
testCases.steps:
1. PUT /api/v1/territories/{Territory B id}/coverage including FL.
2. Inspect status and message.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 with message 'Coverage already exists for US:FL' (validateCoverageConflicts; unique countryCode_stateCode constraint); Territory B coverage unchanged and no partial write (validation runs before the transaction).

testCases.title: Duplicate state codes in one coverage request are de-duplicated
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. A territory with no coverage.
testCases.steps:
1. PUT /api/v1/territories/{id}/coverage with [FL, FL, fl] (case/dup variants).
2. Inspect resulting coverage rows.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; coverage contains exactly one US:FL row (Map keyed by countryCode:stateCode de-duplicates); no unique-constraint error.

testCases.title: Invalid state code in coverage list is rejected before any write
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. A territory with existing coverage [GA].
testCases.steps:
1. PUT /api/v1/territories/{id}/coverage with [FL, 'NOTASTATE'].
2. Inspect status and message.
3. Re-read territory coverage.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 'State/Province must be a valid US state or Canadian province'; existing [GA] coverage preserved unchanged (error thrown during normalization, before deleteMany).

testCases.title: Replace coverage with empty list clears all coverage
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. A territory with coverage [FL,SC].
testCases.steps:
1. PUT /api/v1/territories/{id}/coverage with coverage:[].
2. Inspect 200 and coverage.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; all coverage rows removed; afterData coverage=[]; no createMany executed; audit entry written.

testCases.title: Read and update territory policy flags
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. Policy 'default' is seeded.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/territories/policy and note flags.
2. PATCH /api/v1/territories/policy toggling assignNationalTmLeadsByDefault and strategicGrowthRetainsOwnership.
3. GET again to confirm.
testCases.expectedResult: GET returns seeded defaults (preHandoffTmVisibility=false, assignNationalTmLeadsByDefault=true, strategicGrowthRetainsOwnership=true). PATCH returns 200 with updated flags; UPDATE audit entry with before/after; lead assignments refreshed (policy_refresh).

testCases.title: Territory Manager cannot update territory policy
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as TERRITORY_MANAGER.
testCases.steps:
1. PATCH /api/v1/territories/policy with a flag change.
2. Inspect status.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 403 (territory.admin required, TM lacks it); policy unchanged.

testCases.title: TM sees only own-book leads pre-handoff; flag flip immediately widens scope
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as TERRITORY_MANAGER owning lead L1 (stage NEW, not active, not override) and lead L2 (stage CUSTOMER_ACTIVE). Policy preHandoffTmVisibility=false.
testCases.steps:
1. As TM, list leads in territory scope; note L1 excluded, L2 included.
2. As SUPER_ADMIN PATCH policy preHandoffTmVisibility=true.
3. As TM, immediately re-list leads (no service restart).
testCases.expectedResult: Step 1: only L2 visible (visibility gate requires CUSTOMER_ACTIVE or MANUAL_OVERRIDE). Step 3: both L1 and L2 visible on the next request — policy read is non-cached at query time (NFR-TR-003).

testCases.title: RD sees all territories/leads/accounts within their region only
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR of Region X (with territories T1,T2). Region Y exists with territory T3.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/territories as the RD.
2. Confirm T1,T2 present and T3 absent.
testCases.expectedResult: Response includes T1,T2 (region directed by RD, or leads/accounts with assignedRdUserId = RD) and excludes T3 from Region Y (buildRegionalDirectorScope).

testCases.title: Global-visibility roles see all territories with no scope filter
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as EXECUTIVE (or SUPER_ADMIN / ADMIN_CSR_OPS).
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/territories.
2. Compare count to total territories in DB.
testCases.expectedResult: All territories returned with no territory scope filter (hasGlobalRecordVisibility true -> buildTerritoryReadScope returns undefined).

testCases.title: Reassign a lead to a territory with mandatory reason and override method
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR with reassign rights. Lead L is visible to the actor; target territory T is active and in scope.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/leads/{leadId} with territoryId=T and reasonCode.
2. Inspect 200 response.
3. GET /api/v1/territories/history?entityType=lead&entityId={leadId}.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; TerritoryAssignmentOverride upserted; lead.territoryAssignmentMethod=MANUAL_OVERRIDE; UPDATE audit entry (operation territory.reassign_lead); assignment history shows new entry with prior owner, new owner, method and reason.

testCases.title: Reassignment without reasonCode is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR. Visible lead and in-scope target territory.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/leads/{leadId} with territoryId but no reasonCode (or blank).
2. Inspect status and message.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 with message 'reasonCode is required' (requireText); no override written, no audit entry — mandatory-reason rule enforced.

testCases.title: Reassign non-existent lead returns 404
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR.
testCases.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/leads/non-existent-id with a valid body.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 404 { error:'NOT_FOUND', detail:'Lead not found' }; no mutation.

testCases.title: Reassign to an inactive or unknown target territory is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. A visible lead. A territory that is isActive=false.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/leads/{leadId} with territoryId = inactive territory.
2. Inspect status and message.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 'Unknown, inactive, or inaccessible territory' (requireVisibleTargetTerritory requires isActive=true and in-scope); lead unchanged.

testCases.title: TM cannot reassign a lead outside their visible scope (IDOR)
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as TERRITORY_MANAGER. Lead L belongs to a different TM and is not pre-handoff visible.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/leads/{L id} with a valid in-scope target territory and reason.
2. Inspect status.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 403 'Requested lead territory reassignment is outside your visible scope' (assertTerritoryReassignmentVisible); the lead is NOT reassigned — prevents cross-book record theft.

testCases.title: Reassign rejects named TM owner whose role is not TERRITORY_MANAGER
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. Visible lead, in-scope active territory, and a user whose role is REGIONAL_DIRECTOR passed as assignedTmUserId.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/leads/{leadId} with assignedTmUserId = the RD user.
2. Inspect status and message.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 'Selected user must have role TERRITORY_MANAGER'; no override persisted.

testCases.title: Reassign an account to a different territory with reason and audit
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR. Visible account A; in-scope active target territory T.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/accounts/{accountId} with territoryId and reasonCode.
2. Inspect 200.
3. GET history?entityType=account&entityId={accountId}.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; account override upserted; MANUAL_OVERRIDE method; UPDATE audit entry; account assignment history reflects before/after owner and reason.

testCases.title: Bulk reassign leads succeeds atomically and de-duplicates ids
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR. Three visible leads L1,L2,L3; in-scope target territory T.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/leads/bulk with leadIds [L1, L2, L2, L3, '  '] and reasonCode.
2. Inspect 200 response and affected count.
3. Confirm each lead now points to T.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; ids trimmed and de-duplicated to {L1,L2,L3}; all three reassigned to T within one $transaction; bulk audit metadata records leadCount=3.

testCases.title: Bulk reassign rolls back entire batch when one lead id is missing
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR. Leads L1,L2 exist; L_missing does not.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/leads/bulk with leadIds [L1, L2, L_missing].
2. Inspect status and message.
3. Re-read L1 and L2 assignments.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 'Lead not found: L_missing' raised before the transaction; L1 and L2 remain unchanged — no partial commit (NFR-TR-009).

testCases.title: Bulk reassign with empty id list is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/leads/bulk with leadIds [] (or only whitespace ids).
2. Inspect status.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 'At least one lead is required'; no transaction started.

testCases.title: Bulk reassign accounts between territories atomically
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR. Visible accounts A1,A2; in-scope active target territory T.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/accounts/bulk with accountIds [A1,A2] and reasonCode.
2. Inspect 200.
3. Confirm both accounts now point to T.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; both accounts reassigned in one transaction; bulk audit records accountCount=2; UX bulk account transfer flow confirmed Done (UX-TR-008).

testCases.title: Bulk account reassign with one missing account id aborts batch
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR. A1 exists; A_missing does not.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/territories/assignments/accounts/bulk with accountIds [A1, A_missing].
2. Inspect status and message.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 400 'Account not found: A_missing'; A1 unchanged; no partial commit.

testCases.title: Assignment history is returned newest-first and is immutable
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. A lead reassigned at least twice.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/territories/history?entityType=lead&entityId={leadId}.
2. Inspect ordering and fields.
3. Attempt (via API surface) to mutate or delete a history record.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; history entries ordered changedAt desc, each carrying prior owner, new owner, method, reasonCode/reasonNote and changedByUser; no API path exists to update or delete history records (immutable, NFR-TR-010).

testCases.title: History request with missing or invalid entityType is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/territories/history with no entityId.
2. GET /api/v1/territories/history?entityType=widget&entityId=x.
testCases.testData: Case A: entityType=lead only. Case B: entityType=widget&entityId=x
testCases.expectedResult: Case A: HTTP 400 'entityType and entityId are required'. Case B: HTTP 400 'entityType must be lead, account, or location'.

testCases.title: TM cannot read assignment history for an out-of-scope account
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as TERRITORY_MANAGER. Account belongs to another TM's book.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/territories/history?entityType=account&entityId={out-of-scope account id}.
2. Inspect status.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 403 'Requested account territory history is outside your visible scope' (assertTerritoryAssignmentHistoryVisible); no history leaked.

testCases.title: Dashboard returns full posture payload scoped to the viewer
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR with at least one region of territories, leads, and accounts.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/territories/dashboard.
2. Inspect the response object for required sections.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; response includes stats, coverage, lifecycle, pipeline, training penetration, alert queue, workload, region rollups, owner metrics, and queue summary (territoriesMissingManager, territoriesMissingShippingCenter, regionsMissingDirector) — all scoped to the RD's region.

testCases.title: Territories with no manager or shipping center surface as hygiene items
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as SUPER_ADMIN. A territory with managerUserId=null and shippingCenterId=null; a region with directorUserId=null.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/territories/dashboard.
2. Inspect queue summary counts.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200 (no error despite nulls); territoriesMissingManager, territoriesMissingShippingCenter and regionsMissingDirector counts each reflect the unowned records — data degrades safely (NFR-TR-007).

testCases.title: Next-work item queue renders but drill-through is not yet wired
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as a territory role on the web command dashboard with at least one next-work item.
testCases.steps:
1. Open the Territory Command Dashboard.
2. Confirm next-work items render with tone, owner, gap label and location label.
3. Click a next-work item.
testCases.expectedResult: Items render correctly; clicking currently performs NO drill-through navigation — this gap (UX-TR-001) is Open. Test documents expected future behavior (navigate to the underlying record).

testCases.title: Region rollup rows render but are not expandable to territory list
testCases.preconditions: Logged in on the web command dashboard with multiple regions.
testCases.steps:
1. Open the dashboard region rollup section.
2. Confirm one row per region with rollup metrics.
3. Attempt to expand a region row to its territory list.
testCases.expectedResult: Region rollup rows display; expansion to the territory list is NOT available (UX-TR-005 Open). Test asserts current state and documents target expand behavior.

testCases.title: Map workspace renders state boundaries, shipping centers, pins and hover tooltips
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as a territory role on the Territory Coverage Map page with coverage, shipping centers, and lead/account pins present.
testCases.steps:
1. Open the territory map.
2. Confirm MapLibre renders GeoJSON state boundaries with approved territory colors.
3. Confirm shipping-center warehouse markers render.
4. Confirm lead/account pins render with status color coding.
5. Hover a state.
testCases.expectedResult: State boundaries colored via resolvePaperMapTerritoryStyle; shipping-center markers clickable; pins rendered with status colors; hover popup shows territory name, assigned TM, assigned RD, and shipping center.

testCases.title: Map mode selector and pin drill-through work for office and field users
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as an office/leadership role (e.g. EXECUTIVE) and separately as a TM, on the map page.
testCases.steps:
1. Switch map mode through coverage, accounts, pipeline, all.
2. Click a lead pin and an account pin.
3. Repeat as the office-side user.
testCases.expectedResult: Mode selector filters layers correctly; clicking a pin drills through to the lead/account record (UX-TR-009 Done); map is usable by both field TMs and office/leadership users (FR-TR-032).

testCases.title: State-level-coverage-only context banner is not yet present on the map
testCases.preconditions: Logged in on the Territory Coverage Map page.
testCases.steps:
1. Open the map.
2. Look for a banner communicating 'state-level coverage only' Phase-1 precision.
testCases.expectedResult: No state-level coverage banner is shown — FR-TR-031 is Not-built (UX-TR-004 Open). Test documents the expected banner copy for when it is implemented.

testCases.title: Filtered territory list with zero results shows no empty-state placeholder
testCases.preconditions: Logged in on the Territory Management UI; apply a filter that matches no territories.
testCases.steps:
1. Apply a filter yielding zero territories.
2. Observe the list area.
testCases.expectedResult: List renders empty with NO dedicated empty-state placeholder — FR-TR-038 Not-built (UX-TR-003 Open). Test documents target empty-state messaging.

testCases.title: Assignable-users list returns only TM and RD role users
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR. Users of various roles exist (TM, RD, FINANCE, SALES_BD_REP).
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/territories/assignable-users.
2. Inspect the returned roleCodes.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200; only users with roleCode TERRITORY_MANAGER or REGIONAL_DIRECTOR are returned; FINANCE/SALES users excluded (ASSIGNABLE_TERRITORY_ROLE_CODES filter).

testCases.title: Training session check-in and check-out from the map workspace
testCases.preconditions: Logged in as a TM/RD on the Territory Coverage Map page with a scheduled training session at a mapped account.
testCases.steps:
