3. Create asset with title of only non-alphanumeric chars ('!!!---').
testCases.expectedResult: Slugify lowercases, strips non a-z0-9 to hyphens, trims edge hyphens; an all-symbol title yields a randomUUID slug (never empty). Title stored verbatim (trimmed); HTML is stored as data, not executed. Widen-derived slugs are truncated to 180 chars. No crash or constraint violation.

testCases.title: Concurrent accesses to the same share token increment accessCount atomically
testCases.preconditions: Active share link with accessCount=0.
testCases.steps:
1. Fire 10 concurrent GET /shares/{token} requests.
2. Re-read accessCount.
testCases.expectedResult: accessCount equals 10 (atomic {increment:1} avoids lost updates); each request returns 302. No race causes an undercount or a server error.

testCases.title: Legacy Widen URL redirect activation is parked (aliases stored as pending only)

testCases.expectedResult: Aliases persist with redirectStatus='pending'; no live redirect occurs yet. Activation/cutover is Parked pending the migration plan — test documents the dependency; redirect behaviour is not expected to function until activated.

testCases.feature: Dealer/TM Access — Native mobile app (not built)
testCases.title: Dedicated React Native digital-assets screen for TMs

testCases.steps:

testCases.expectedResult: No dedicated native Digital Assets screen exists yet — this scenario is expected to be unavailable until built. Tracks the gap; verify only the CRM-web mobile fallback in DAM-TC-034 for current coverage.

testCases.title: Acumatica health endpoint returns ok payload when ERP reachable
testCases.preconditions: Acumatica sandbox/stub reachable so $metadata responds 200. API running. Health endpoint /api/v1/health/acumatica wired (server.ts).
testCases.steps:
1. Issue GET /api/v1/health/acumatica.
2. Inspect HTTP status and JSON body.
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 200. Body is {ok:true, statusCode:200, endpoint:'<base>/entity/24.100.001/<company>/$metadata', checkedAt:<ISO8601>}. Response returns within 5 seconds (NFR-ACU-013).

testCases.title: Acumatica health endpoint returns 503 with error detail when ERP unreachable
testCases.preconditions: Acumatica base URL unreachable / login refused (default placeholder host or network failure).
testCases.steps:
1. Issue GET /api/v1/health/acumatica with Acumatica down.
2. Inspect status and body.
testCases.testData: ACUMATICA_BASE_URL pointing at an unreachable host
testCases.expectedResult: HTTP 503. Body has ok:false, statusCode (e.g. 503 on thrown fetch error), endpoint set, checkedAt set, and an error string carrying the failure message. Pulse itself does not crash (graceful degradation, NFR-ACU-008).

testCases.title: Admin integration-status shows Acumatica card with health and last-checked timestamp
testCases.preconditions: Admin/Ops user authenticated. GET admin integration-status endpoint available (admin/service.ts getAdminIntegrationStatus).
testCases.steps:
1. As Admin, fetch the admin integration-status endpoint.
2. Locate the integration entry with key='acumatica'.
testCases.expectedResult: Response.integrations contains {key:'acumatica', label:'Acumatica', status, health, lastCheckedAt, detail}. When ERP healthy: status='connected', health=100. When down: status='warning', health=45, detail='Awaiting sandbox certification or upstream access.' (never status='error', confirming graceful degradation).

testCases.title: Acumatica down surfaces as warning (not error) and does not fail the whole dashboard
testCases.preconditions: Acumatica unreachable; database and queue healthy. Admin user authenticated.
testCases.steps:

2. Fetch admin integration-status.
testCases.expectedResult: Dashboard returns 200 with full integration list; acumatica entry status='warning' health=45; database/queue entries unaffected (status='connected'). No hard failure (NFR-ACU-008).

testCases.title: Client prefers Bearer token over cookie session when accessToken configured
testCases.preconditions: AcumaticaClient constructed with accessToken set (and optionally username/password).
testCases.steps:
1. Construct client with accessToken.
2. Invoke a GET; capture outbound request headers via fetch stub.
testCases.expectedResult: Outbound request carries header authorization='Bearer tok_abc' and NO cookie header. Bearer path takes precedence over session cookie (client.ts headers()).

testCases.title: Client performs cookie-session login and reuses Set-Cookie on subsequent calls
testCases.preconditions: Client constructed with username+password, no accessToken. Fetch stub returns set-cookie on /entity/auth/login.
testCases.steps:
1. Call login().
2. Issue a subsequent GET.
3. Inspect headers of the GET.
testCases.expectedResult: login() POSTs {name,password,company} to /entity/auth/login; on success the returned set-cookie is stored and the next request includes header cookie=<stored cookie>. No authorization Bearer header sent.

testCases.title: login() throws when username or password missing
testCases.preconditions: Client constructed without username/password and without accessToken.
testCases.steps: 1. Call client.login().
testCases.expectedResult: login() throws Error('Acumatica credentials are missing'). No HTTP request is made.

testCases.title: Cookie-session client auto-re-logs-in once on 401 then replays the request
testCases.preconditions: Client with username/password, no accessToken. Fetch stub returns 401 on first entity call, 200 after a fresh login.
testCases.steps:
1. Issue a GET that first returns 401.
2. Observe re-login and replay.
testCases.testData: First response 401, then login 200, then entity 200
testCases.expectedResult: On 401 (no accessToken, creds present) the client calls login() and retries the original request exactly once, returning the 200 body. (Note: only single-retry on 401 is built; full 3x exp-backoff circuit-breaker per FR-ACU-039 is parked.)

testCases.title: Bearer-auth client does NOT auto-re-login on 401 (no credentials to log in with)
testCases.preconditions: Client constructed with accessToken only (no username/password). Fetch stub returns 401.
testCases.steps: 1. Issue a GET that returns 401.
testCases.expectedResult: Client does not attempt login (guarded by !accessToken && username && password); it throws AcumaticaClientError with statusCode 401. No infinite retry loop.

testCases.title: Non-2xx response is normalized into AcumaticaClientError carrying statusCode and payload
testCases.preconditions: Fetch stub returns 500 with JSON error body {message, exceptionMessage}.
testCases.steps:
1. Issue a GET that returns 500 with an error body.
2. Catch the thrown error.
testCases.expectedResult: AcumaticaClientError thrown with .statusCode=500 and .payload containing the parsed error object. message resolves to payload.message || exceptionMessage || fallback. No credentials present in the error payload.

testCases.title: Error response with non-JSON body falls back to text without throwing a parse error
testCases.preconditions: Fetch stub returns 502 with a plain-text/HTML body (no valid JSON).
testCases.steps:
1. Issue a request returning a 502 HTML body.
2. Catch the error.
testCases.expectedResult: asClientError catches the JSON parse failure and falls back to response.text(); an AcumaticaClientError is thrown (no unhandled SyntaxError). statusCode=502.

testCases.title: Endpoint base is built from base URL, pinned API version, and company

testCases.title: OData $select/$expand/$filter are serialized as query params; undefined values skipped

testCases.steps:

testCases.expectedResult: Request URL includes ?$select=CustomerID&$filter=CreditHold+eq+true (URL-encoded); $expand omitted because its value is undefined. Confirms OData param plumbing.

testCases.title: 204 No Content response returns undefined without attempting to parse a body
testCases.preconditions: Fetch stub returns 204 for a DELETE.
testCases.steps: 1. Call client.delete('Customer/...') against a 204 stub.
testCases.expectedResult: Call resolves to undefined; no JSON parse is attempted on the empty body; no error thrown.

testCases.title: New consignment site is created with acumaticaStatus=PARKED and never an invented warehouse ID

testCases.title: Pulse never auto-generates acumaticaWarehouseId; status stays PARKED until ERP returns real ID

testCases.title: Transitioning a site to READY_FOR_WAREHOUSE creates a BLOCKED WAREHOUSE_SETUP work item

testCases.title: Site cannot be activated without a warehouse reference (plus agreement and BLUE baseline)

testCases.expectedResult: Update rejected with error listing blockers including 'warehouse reference' (and 'signed agreement', 'BLUE baseline evidence' as applicable). Site stays non-ACTIVE. Enforces Acumatica-originated warehouse precondition.

testCases.title: PO received true-up records manual reference only; no Acumatica PO is posted

NO POST /PurchaseOrder is sent to Acumatica (parked). When sandbox certified, expectation flips to a real POST with pending_acumatica status.

testCases.title: Inventory baseline recalculation remains Pulse-manual; not gated on a live Acumatica PO confirmation

testCases.title: PURPLE inventory adjustment updates Pulse manual baseline only; Acumatica post is parked

testCases.title: SAND exit closes site in Pulse with manual reconciliation; Acumatica settlement post parked

testCases.title: Consignment inventory-value KPI is returned as a Parked card in Reports

testCases.title: Failed customer creation retries up to 3x with back-off and surfaces a sync-error badge

testCases.title: Credit-hold sync uses 15-min polling default or push notifications when certified
testCases.preconditions: DEPENDS ON Acumatica push notifications (documented in 2024 R2 docs, unconfirmed in DAQS instance) or polling (parked).
testCases.steps:
1. Configure the polling interval.
2. Trigger a credit-hold change and measure latency to the Pulse badge.
testCases.expectedResult: Per NFR-ACU-002 latency must not exceed 15 minutes via polling; push path reduces to under 60 seconds once certified. Push availability must be confirmed in sandbox (ASM-ACU-007 correction). Parked.

testCases.title: Acumatica-sourced status shows a stale-data warning when lastSyncedAt > 30 minutes
testCases.preconditions: DEPENDS ON live Acumatica reads writing lastSyncedAt (parked for accounts/products; pattern established in consignment).
testCases.steps:
1. Make an Acumatica-sourced field have lastSyncedAt older than 30 minutes.
2. Inspect the UI badge.
testCases.expectedResult: Per FR-ACU-037 a stale-data warning is shown when lastSyncedAt > 30 minutes and suppressed when current. The stale-data pattern exists in consignment but is not yet applied to accounts/product fields — partial per PRD.

testCases.title: Account priceClassCode is not yet fetched live from Acumatica CustomerClass
testCases.preconditions: DEPENDS ON Acumatica CustomerClass/PriceClassID read (parked). priceClassCode field exists in leads contract.
testCases.steps:
1. Inspect priceClassCode on the leads/account contract.
2. Check whether it is populated from a live Acumatica read.
testCases.expectedResult: priceClassCode field exists (partial) but is not populated from a live Acumatica read; price-class resolution (Affinity+Ownership+Region→Dealer Group→Price Class) stays in Acumatica (ASM-ACU-005). Live read is parked.

testCases.feature: Dealer portal price resolution + manual sync (parked)
testCases.title: Dealer portal prices resolve by the dealer's Acumatica price class; admin manual sync available
testCases.preconditions: DEPENDS ON Acumatica price-book read by price class (parked). Logged-in dealer with a priceClassCode.
testCases.steps:
1. As a dealer, view a product price.
2. As Admin, trigger 'Sync from Acumatica' price-class sync on the account.
testCases.expectedResult: Per FR-ACU-014 product prices match the price book for the dealer's priceClassCode; per FR-ACU-016 an admin 'Sync from Acumatica' action updates the badge. Both parked — not built.

testCases.title: Checkout queries real-time Acumatica inventory; zero-quantity items show Out of stock
testCases.preconditions: DEPENDS ON Acumatica real-time inventory query (parked). Dealer at checkout with an out-of-stock item.
testCases.steps: 1. As a dealer, add a zero-quantity SKU and attempt checkout.
testCases.expectedResult: Per FR-ACU-022 product displays 'Out of stock' and checkout is blocked for zero-quantity items unless back-order is allowed; single-warehouse inventory read returns within 3 seconds (NFR-ACU-003). Parked — not built.

testCases.title: Publishing dealer catalog is blocked when legacy CSV-seed (FILE_IMPORT) products are present
testCases.preconditions: Actor has product.publish. Catalog view includes at least one BaseProduct with sourceSystem=FILE_IMPORT (legacy seed, not Acumatica-reconciled).
testCases.steps: 1. Attempt publishDealerCatalogSnapshot for a catalog view containing a FILE_IMPORT product.
testCases.expectedResult: Publish throws: 'Cannot publish: N product(s) are legacy-seed imports not yet reconciled with Acumatica (e.g. LEGACY-001)...'. No snapshot is created. Enforces FR-ACU-031 (publish blocked while acumaticaInventoryId is from legacy CSV seed).

testCases.title: Publishing succeeds when all catalog products are Acumatica-reconciled (no FILE_IMPORT)
testCases.preconditions: Actor has product.publish. Catalog view has only products with certified acumaticaInventoryId and at least one approved dealer-safe file each.
testCases.steps: 1. publishDealerCatalogSnapshot for a fully reconciled catalog view.
testCases.testData: Catalog view, all products non-FILE_IMPORT, each with >=1 approved file
testCases.expectedResult: Snapshot is created successfully; no legacy-seed error. Confirms the gate only blocks unreconciled legacy items.

testCases.title: Products expose read-only acumaticaInventoryId/acumaticaItemClass/acumaticaLastSyncedAt
testCases.preconditions: Product-management module accessible; a base product exists.
testCases.steps:
1. Read a product record and its mapped contract.
2. Attempt to edit acumaticaInventoryId via the product update path.
testCases.expectedResult: acumaticaInventoryId, acumaticaItemClass, acumaticaLastSyncedAt are present and treated as read-only/Acumatica-owned identity fields (base/list price excluded per 2026-06-18 correction — price originates in the external pricing engine). Live API sync to refresh them is parked.

testCases.title: Initial product import via CSV seeds base records; live API delta-sync remains parked
testCases.preconditions: CSV export 'Acumatica Stock Items.xlsx' available; product-management legacy-import path built.
testCases.steps:
1. Run the CSV import path to seed base products.
2. Verify products land with sourceSystem=FILE_IMPORT.
3. Confirm no live API delta-sync runs.
testCases.expectedResult: CSV import seeds base records (built, legacy-import.ts); imported records carry FILE_IMPORT source (so they are blocked from publish per ACU-TC-038). Periodic live API delta-sync (FR-ACU-032) is parked — no nightly delta job runs.

testCases.title: Account ERP Orders tab shows a placeholder; no live Acumatica order/invoice history
testCases.preconditions: DEPENDS ON Acumatica order/invoice/shipment read (parked). Account detail page open (CustomerDetail.tsx placeholder).
testCases.steps: 1. Open account detail and the ERP Orders tab.
testCases.expectedResult: Per FR-ACU-028 the tab should show up to 12 months of read-only order history with links out to Acumatica. Currently a placeholder card is present and no live history is fetched — parked.

testCases.title: Pulse never writes Acumatica financial fields (order, invoice, AR balance, credit limit)
testCases.preconditions: Any authenticated role; account with (future) Acumatica-sourced financial fields.
testCases.steps:
1. Inspect all account/consignment write paths for any PUT/POST targeting order, invoice, AR balance, or credit-limit fields.
2. Attempt to edit a read-only ERP financial field via the account update contract.
testCases.testData: Attempt to set arBalance / creditLimit via account update
testCases.expectedResult: No Pulse write path mutates Acumatica financial truth; ERP financial fields are read-only/absent from update contracts (NFR-ACU-011, ASM-ACU-009). Attempted edits are ignored or rejected.

testCases.title: Acumatica credentials are read from env only and never appear in logs or error payloads
testCases.preconditions: Acumatica env keys configured (ACUMATICA_USERNAME/PASSWORD/ACCESS_TOKEN). Trigger a failing Acumatica call.
testCases.steps:
1. Force an Acumatica error and capture the AcumaticaClientError + any structured logs.
2. grep source/DB for hardcoded credentials.
testCases.testData: Failing Acumatica request with creds configured
testCases.expectedResult: Credentials sourced only from env (packages/config env.ts). Error payload and any logs contain statusCode/entity/message but NO username, password, or token (NFR-ACU-004/010). No credential literals committed in source or DB.

testCases.title: No Pulse feature hard-fails when Acumatica is unreachable
testCases.preconditions: Acumatica unreachable. Exercise consignment, accounts, and product modules.
testCases.steps: 1. With Acumatica down, create a consignment site, open an account detail, and view the product catalog.
testCases.expectedResult: All flows complete using parked-status placeholders; consignment site creates with acumaticaStatus=PARKED, account placeholder cards render, product module functions. No request blocks or 5xx caused by Acumatica being down (NFR-ACU-008).

testCases.title: Territory Manager sees and mutates only consignment sites they own (ownerTmUserId)
testCases.preconditions: Two consignment sites: Site A owned by TM-1, Site B owned by TM-2. Authenticated as TM-1.
testCases.steps:
1. As TM-1, list consignment sites.
2. Attempt to fetch/mutate Site B by ID (IDOR attempt).
testCases.testData: TM-1 session; Site B owned by TM-2
testCases.expectedResult: List returns only Site A (siteScopeWhere = {ownerTmUserId: self}). getSiteForMutation for Site B throws 'Consignment site not found' (scoped 404, no leak). TM cannot read or write another TM's site.

testCases.title: Regional Director sees sites they own or that belong to their region only
testCases.preconditions: Sites in Region-1 (RD-1 director) and Region-2. Authenticated as RD-1.
testCases.steps:
1. As RD-1, list consignment sites.
2. Attempt to access a Region-2 site by ID.
testCases.expectedResult: List returns sites where ownerRdUserId=RD-1 OR region.directorUserId=RD-1. Region-2 site access throws 'Consignment site not found'. Confirms RD scoping (siteScopeWhere).

testCases.title: Dealer-portal user is denied access to internal consignment/Acumatica workflow endpoints
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated as DEALER_PORTAL_USER.
testCases.steps: 1. As a dealer-portal user, call a consignment endpoint (list/detail/manage).
testCases.expectedResult: Authorization error thrown: 'Consignment is internal-only in the current phase' (assertConsignmentAccess). Dealer portal users have no access to internal consignment/Acumatica workflow records (default-deny).

testCases.title: Executive can view consignment but cannot manage workflow records (incl. warehouse setup)
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated as EXECUTIVE.
testCases.steps:
1. As Executive, view consignment sites (allowed).
2. Attempt to create/update a consignment site or transition to READY_FOR_WAREHOUSE.
testCases.expectedResult: View succeeds; any manage action throws 'Executive role can view consignment but cannot manage workflow records' (assertConsignmentManage). Executives cannot trigger the Acumatica warehouse-setup work item.

testCases.title: Manual Acumatica sync and catalog publish require explicit permission (default-deny for others)
testCases.preconditions: Roles without product.publish / without admin sync rights (e.g. TM, dealer-portal).
testCases.steps:
1. As a non-privileged role, attempt publishDealerCatalogSnapshot.
2. Attempt the admin 'Sync from Acumatica' action (FR-ACU-016).
testCases.expectedResult: Both actions are denied via assertActionAccess('product.publish') / admin guard — default-deny. Only authorized Admin/Ops (and product roles for publish) may invoke Acumatica sync/publish actions.

testCases.title: Consignment document/notes reject raw payment card numbers (PCI boundary)
testCases.preconditions: Actor with consignment.document_manage. Notes field used on a consignment document.
testCases.steps: 1. Submit a consignment document whose notes contain a raw 16-digit PAN.
testCases.expectedResult: assertNoRawPaymentCardData rejects the input with a PCI-rejection error; the document is not persisted. Confirms Pulse never stores raw card data (PCI boundary; payment tokens only).

testCases.title: Concurrent first-order triggers must not race into two Acumatica customer creations
testCases.preconditions: DEPENDS ON Acumatica Customer endpoint + idempotency (parked). Two simultaneous first-order activations for the same account.
testCases.steps:
1. Fire two concurrent first-order triggers for the same account.
2. Inspect resulting customer records.
testCases.expectedResult: Per FR-ACU-002 idempotency, concurrent triggers must resolve to a single Acumatica customer (idempotency key / unique guard prevents a TOCTOU double-create). Parked — verify atomic guard once built.

testCases.title: Customer-creation payload requires mapped fields and valid contact email/phone formats
testCases.preconditions: DEPENDS ON Acumatica Customer endpoint + field-mapping (FR-ACU-042, parked). Account missing required mapped fields.
testCases.steps: 1. Trigger customer creation for an account missing legal name / invalid contact email.
testCases.expectedResult: Per FR-ACU-042 mapping (AccountNumber→CustomerID, legalName→CustomerName, email→CustomerContact), required fields must be present and email/phone validly formatted before any Acumatica PUT. Parked — validation enforced once mapping is built.

testCases.title: No entity is written to Acumatica until $metadata schema and NAW.DAQS custom fields are documented
testCases.preconditions: DEPENDS ON sandbox $metadata query + field-mapping doc sign-off (FR-ACU-007/041/044; gates G2-G4 open).
testCases.steps:
1. Verify that no production code writes Customer/Warehouse/StockItem entities.
2. Confirm the field-mapping doc / $metadata capture is a precondition.
testCases.expectedResult: All entity-write paths remain parked until G2 ($metadata captured), G3 (NAW.DAQS custom fields listed), and G4 (mapping doc approved by Dan Harshbarger/Finance). No Acumatica writes occur before certification. Documents the hard pre-sprint gate.

testCases.title: List own notifications returns items, total and unreadCount
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated user (any signed-in role — every user has an inbox, no module gate). User has >=3 in-app notifications materialized via the bridge.
testCases.steps:
1. Sign in and obtain a valid bearer token.
2. GET /api/v1/notifications
testCases.expectedResult: 200 with { items[], total, unreadCount }. items ordered by createdAt desc, each item exposes id, category, eventType, severity, title, isRead, createdAt and (when present) body/deepLinkType/deepLinkId. total and unreadCount are integers reflecting only the actor's own rows.

testCases.title: Filter list by status=unread / archived / all
testCases.preconditions: Actor has a mix of read, unread, and archived notifications.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/notifications?status=unread
2. GET /api/v1/notifications?status=archived
3. GET /api/v1/notifications?status=all
testCases.testData: status query param: unread | archived | all
testCases.expectedResult: unread → only rows with readAt null and archivedAt null. archived → only rows with archivedAt not null. all (and default) → all non-archived rows (read + unread). Counts in 'total' match the filtered set.

testCases.title: Filter list by valid category enum (lead/consignment/training/order/account/system)
testCases.preconditions: Actor has notifications across multiple categories.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/notifications?category=lead
2. GET /api/v1/notifications?category=consignment
testCases.expectedResult: Only notifications whose category matches the requested enum are returned; total reflects the filtered subset.

testCases.title: Unknown category value is silently ignored (not applied as filter)
testCases.preconditions: Actor has notifications in several categories.
testCases.steps: 1. GET /api/v1/notifications?category=banana
testCases.expectedResult: 200; the invalid category is dropped (handler only applies the filter when value is in the enum), so the response is the unfiltered (status-default) list rather than an error or empty set.

testCases.title: Pagination via limit and offset returns correct page window
testCases.preconditions: Actor has at least 35 non-archived notifications.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/notifications?limit=10&offset=0
2. GET /api/v1/notifications?limit=10&offset=10
testCases.expectedResult: Each call returns exactly 10 items, ordered createdAt desc; the two pages do not overlap; total reflects the full filtered count (not the page size).

testCases.title: limit clamps to MAX_LIMIT (100) and minimum (1)
testCases.preconditions: Actor has >100 notifications.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/notifications?limit=100000
2. GET /api/v1/notifications?limit=0
3. GET /api/v1/notifications?limit=-5
testCases.expectedResult: limit=100000 returns at most 100 items (clamped to MAX_LIMIT). limit=0 and limit=-5 are clamped up to 1 (returns 1 item). No 500.

testCases.title: Negative or non-integer offset handled (floored to 0 / ignored)
testCases.preconditions: Actor has notifications.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/notifications?offset=-50
2. GET /api/v1/notifications?offset=abc
3. GET /api/v1/notifications?limit=abc
testCases.expectedResult: offset=-50 → floored to 0 (first page). offset=abc / limit=abc → Number() yields NaN which is not an integer, so the param is ignored and defaults apply (offset 0, limit 30). No error.

testCases.title: GET unread-count returns count of unread, non-archived notifications
testCases.preconditions: Actor has 4 unread, 2 read, 1 archived(unread-originally) notification.
testCases.steps: 1. GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count
testCases.expectedResult: 200 with { unreadCount: 4 }. Archived rows (even if readAt null) and already-read rows are excluded (where readAt null AND archivedAt null).

testCases.title: Mark specific notification ids as read updates only those and recomputes unread count
testCases.preconditions: Actor has 5 unread notifications; capture ids of 2 of them.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/notifications/mark-read with body { ids: [id1, id2] }
2. GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count
testCases.expectedResult: 200 with { updated: 2, unreadCount: 3 }. Subsequent unread-count confirms 3. The two rows now have readAt set; others unchanged.

testCases.title: Mark-all-read sets every unread notification for the actor to read
testCases.preconditions: Actor has 6 unread notifications.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/notifications/mark-read with body { all: true }
2. GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count
testCases.expectedResult: 200 with { updated: 6, unreadCount: 0 }. all=true ignores ids and updates every unread row for the actor. unread-count is now 0.

testCases.title: Mark-read with empty/absent ids and all falsy is a safe no-op
testCases.preconditions: Actor has unread notifications.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 with { updated: 0, unreadCount: <unchanged current count> } in all three. Empty/blank/non-string ids are filtered out leaving zero valid ids → no update performed.

testCases.title: Re-marking an already-read notification does not change its readAt or count
testCases.preconditions: Notification id1 is already read.
testCases.steps:
1. Note current readAt of id1.
2. POST /api/v1/notifications/mark-read { ids: [id1] }
testCases.expectedResult: 200 with { updated: 0, ... } — the where clause restricts to readAt null, so an already-read row is not matched; original readAt preserved.

testCases.title: Archive a notification sets archivedAt and removes it from default and unread lists
testCases.preconditions: Actor owns unread notification id1.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/notifications/<id1>/archive
2. GET /api/v1/notifications (default)
3. GET /api/v1/notifications?status=archived
testCases.expectedResult: 200 returning the updated summary with archivedAt set and readAt set (archiving an unread item also marks it read). id1 absent from default list, present in status=archived list, and excluded from unread-count.

testCases.title: Archiving an already-archived notification preserves the original archivedAt/readAt
testCases.preconditions: Notification id1 already archived at time T with readAt R.
testCases.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/notifications/<id1>/archive again
testCases.expectedResult: 200; archivedAt stays T and readAt stays R (update uses existing.archivedAt ?? now / existing.readAt ?? now), so re-archiving does not overwrite original timestamps.

testCases.title: Archive a non-existent notification id returns 404
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated actor.
testCases.testData: path id = random uuid not owned / not existing
testCases.expectedResult: 404 not-found with entity 'UserNotification' and the supplied id (findFirst scoped to recipientUserId returns null → notFoundResponse).

testCases.title: Per-recipient read state: one recipient reading a shared alert leaves it unread for others
testCases.preconditions: A shared event (e.g. lead ROUTING_BROADCAST) materialized a separate UserNotification row for User A and User B (distinct rows, same source alert).
testCases.steps:
1. As User A, POST /api/v1/notifications/mark-read { all: true }.
2. As User B, GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count.
testCases.testData: Two users A and B both recipients of the same source alert
testCases.expectedResult: User B's unread-count still includes the shared notification (rows are per-recipient with independent readAt). User A's copy is read; User B's is untouched — supports 'whoever is at their computer makes the call'.

testCases.title: Actor cannot view another user's notifications (list is strictly self-scoped)
testCases.preconditions: User A and User B each have their own notifications.
testCases.steps:
1. Sign in as User A.
2. GET /api/v1/notifications.
testCases.testData: User A token; User B has rows in DB
testCases.expectedResult: Response contains only User A's rows (where recipientUserId = actor.userId). No User B notification leaks; there is no parameter to request another user's inbox.

testCases.title: Actor cannot archive a notification belonging to another user (IDOR)
testCases.preconditions: Notification id-B belongs to User B.
testCases.steps:
1. Sign in as User A.
2. POST /api/v1/notifications/<id-B>/archive.
testCases.testData: User A token; path id = User B's notification id
testCases.expectedResult: 404 not-found (archive lookup is scoped to recipientUserId = actor.userId, so a cross-user id is treated as not found and never mutated). No state change to User B's row.

testCases.title: Mark-read of another user's notification ids has no effect (cross-user ids ignored)
testCases.preconditions: Notification id-B (unread) belongs to User B.
testCases.steps:
1. Sign in as User A.
2. POST /api/v1/notifications/mark-read { ids: [<id-B>] }.
testCases.testData: User A token; ids = [User B's unread notification]
testCases.expectedResult: 200 with { updated: 0, ... } — updateMany where clause requires recipientUserId = User A, so User B's row is not matched. User B's notification remains unread.

testCases.title: All notification endpoints reject requests without a bearer token (401)
testCases.preconditions: No Authorization header / no token.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/notifications (no auth)
2. GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count (no auth)
3. POST /api/v1/notifications/mark-read (no auth)
4. POST /api/v1/notifications/<id>/archive (no auth)
testCases.expectedResult: 401 unauthorized ('Missing bearer token') for each — requireAuthenticatedActor throws AuthenticationError, caught and mapped to unauthorizedResponse.

testCases.title: Invalid or expired bearer token is rejected (401 Invalid session)
testCases.preconditions: A malformed or revoked/expired access token.
testCases.steps: 1. GET /api/v1/notifications with Authorization: Bearer not-a-real-token
testCases.expectedResult: 401 unauthorized ('Invalid session') — authenticateAccessToken returns null → AuthenticationError.

testCases.title: Unsupported HTTP methods return 405 with correct Allow set
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated actor.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/notifications
2. DELETE /api/v1/notifications/unread-count
3. GET /api/v1/notifications/mark-read
4. GET /api/v1/notifications/<id>/archive
testCases.expectedResult: 405 method-not-allowed for each, advertising the allowed methods (list/unread-count → GET; mark-read & archive → POST; preferences → GET,PUT; routing-rules → GET,POST; routing-rules/:id → DELETE).

testCases.title: List preferences returns all 6 categories defaulting to enabled when no row exists
testCases.preconditions: Actor has no UserNotificationPreference rows.
testCases.steps: 1. GET /api/v1/notifications/preferences
testCases.expectedResult: 200 with preferences array of all 6 categories (lead, consignment, training, order, account, system), each inAppEnabled: true (absence of a row = enabled / opt-out model).

testCases.title: Opt out of a category via PUT and confirm it is reflected
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated actor.
testCases.steps:
1. PUT /api/v1/notifications/preferences { category: 'lead', inAppEnabled: false }
2. GET /api/v1/notifications/preferences
testCases.expectedResult: 200; upserts the lead preference to inAppEnabled false. Subsequent list shows lead=false and the other five still true. Re-PUT with true flips it back.

testCases.title: Materialization skips a notification for a category the recipient has muted
testCases.preconditions: User A has opted out of category 'consignment' (inAppEnabled=false). A consignment alert is then scanned where A is a recipient.
testCases.steps:
1. Ensure A's consignment preference is false.
2. Run the consignment alert bridge sync.
3. As A, GET /api/v1/notifications?category=consignment.
testCases.testData: A muted consignment; new consignment alert produced
testCases.expectedResult: No consignment UserNotification row is created for A (upsertUserNotification returns early when isCategoryEnabledForUser is false). A's consignment list stays empty for that event; other recipients who did not opt out still receive it.

testCases.title: PUT preference with missing or invalid category is rejected (400)
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated actor.
testCases.steps:
1. PUT /api/v1/notifications/preferences { inAppEnabled: false } (no category)
2. PUT /api/v1/notifications/preferences { category: 'finance', inAppEnabled: false }
testCases.expectedResult: 400 bad-request 'A valid notification category is required.' for both — handler validates category against USER_NOTIFICATION_CATEGORIES before calling the service.

testCases.title: inAppEnabled is coerced to boolean (truthy/falsy/missing)
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated actor.
testCases.steps:
1. PUT /api/v1/notifications/preferences { category:'order' } (inAppEnabled absent)
2. PUT /api/v1/notifications/preferences { category:'order', inAppEnabled:'yes' }
testCases.expectedResult: Step 1: Boolean(undefined)=false → order muted. Step 2: Boolean('yes')=true → order re-enabled. No 500; value persisted as a strict boolean.

testCases.title: Preferences are per-user; one user's opt-out does not affect another user
testCases.preconditions: User A muted 'lead'; User B has no preferences.
testCases.steps: 1. As B, GET /api/v1/notifications/preferences.
testCases.expectedResult: User B sees lead=true (B has no row). Preference upsert/list key is recipientUserId = actor.userId, so settings never cross users.

testCases.title: Admin creates a role-based routing rule (201)
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated actor with admin-module access.
testCases.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/notifications/routing-rules { category:'lead', eventType:'cis_received', recipientType:'role', recipientRoleCode:'RD' }
testCases.expectedResult: 201 returning the rule summary (id, category lead, eventType cis_received, recipientType role, recipientRoleCode RD, isActive true, createdAt). Rule persisted and listable.

testCases.title: Active role routing rule expands to all active users with that role on next scan
testCases.preconditions: Admin has created an active role rule (category=lead, eventType=cis_received, role=RD). Two active RD users exist; one inactive RD user exists. A lead with cisSubmittedAt set exists.
testCases.steps:
1. Run the CIS-received bridge sync.
2. As each active RD user, GET /api/v1/notifications.
testCases.testData: 2 active RD users + 1 inactive RD user
testCases.expectedResult: Both active RD users receive the cis_received notification (resolveRuleRecipients expands role → active users with that roleCode), unioned with entity defaults (assignee + assigned RD). The inactive RD user receives nothing (isActive:true filter).

testCases.title: Routing rule with no eventType applies to every event in the category
testCases.preconditions: Admin creates a consignment rule with recipientType=user, recipientUserId=U, no eventType.
testCases.steps:
1. POST routing rule { category:'consignment', recipientType:'user', recipientUserId:'<U>' } (eventType omitted)
2. Run consignment bridge for several different consignment alertTypes.
testCases.expectedResult: User U receives a notification for every consignment alertType produced (resolveRuleRecipients OR eventType null OR eventType=<x> matches the null rule for all events).

testCases.title: Create routing rule rejects invalid category and invalid recipientType (400)
testCases.preconditions: Admin actor.
testCases.steps:
1. POST routing-rules { category:'pizza', recipientType:'role', recipientRoleCode:'RD' }
2. POST routing-rules { category:'lead', recipientType:'group', recipientRoleCode:'RD' }
testCases.expectedResult: Step 1 → 400 'A valid notification category is required.' Step 2 → 400 'recipientType must be "role" or "user".'

testCases.title: Role rule without roleCode and user rule without userId are rejected
testCases.preconditions: Admin actor.
testCases.steps:
1. POST routing-rules { category:'lead', recipientType:'role' } (no recipientRoleCode)
2. POST routing-rules { category:'lead', recipientType:'user' } (no recipientUserId)
testCases.testData: role rule missing roleCode; user rule missing userId
testCases.expectedResult: Step 1 → 400 'A recipientRoleCode is required for a role rule.' Step 2 → 400 'A recipientUserId is required for a user rule.' (service throws; mapped to badRequest).

testCases.title: Non-admin user is forbidden from listing/creating routing rules (403 + audit)
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated user WITHOUT admin-module access (e.g. Territory Manager).
testCases.steps:
1. As TM, GET /api/v1/notifications/routing-rules
2. As TM, POST /api/v1/notifications/routing-rules { category:'lead', recipientType:'role', recipientRoleCode:'RD' }
testCases.expectedResult: 403 forbidden for both (requireAuthenticatedActor with module:'admin' → assertModuleAccess throws AuthorizationError). A REJECT AuditEntry (entityType AUTHORIZATION_ATTEMPT) is written capturing actor, role, path and method.

testCases.title: Verify which roles may and may not manage routing rules (default-deny)
testCases.preconditions: Test users for each role: Admin, Regional Director, Territory Manager, Business Development, Finance, Dealer/Customer.
testCases.steps: 1. For each role, attempt GET and POST /api/v1/notifications/routing-rules.
testCases.expectedResult: Only roles granted the admin module succeed (200/201). All others (TM, BD, Finance, RD unless admin-scoped, Dealer) receive 403. Default-deny: any role not explicitly granted admin is rejected.

testCases.title: Admin deletes an existing routing rule (200) and deleting again returns 404
testCases.preconditions: An existing routing rule with id R; admin actor.
testCases.steps:
1. DELETE /api/v1/notifications/routing-rules/<R>
2. DELETE /api/v1/notifications/routing-rules/<R> (again)
testCases.expectedResult: First DELETE → 200 { ok: true } (deleteMany count > 0). Second DELETE → 404 not-found (count 0). After delete, the rule no longer expands recipients in the bridge.

testCases.title: Non-admin cannot delete a routing rule (403)
testCases.preconditions: Existing rule id R; non-admin authenticated user.
testCases.steps: 1. As non-admin, DELETE /api/v1/notifications/routing-rules/<R>
testCases.expectedResult: 403 forbidden (admin-module gate evaluated before delete). Rule R is not deleted; denial audited.

testCases.title: Re-running the bridge does not duplicate a notification (upsert on recipientUserId+dedupeKey)
testCases.preconditions: A lead operational alert exists with recipient U; bridge already ran once.
testCases.steps:
1. Run syncLeadAlertNotifications.
2. Run syncLeadAlertNotifications again (same data).
3. As U, GET /api/v1/notifications?category=lead.
testCases.testData: Same source alert across two scans
testCases.expectedResult: Exactly one UserNotification row for (U, dedupeKey 'lead-alert:<alertId>:<U>'); the second run upserts (refreshes title/severity) rather than inserting a duplicate. Honors the @@unique([recipientUserId, dedupeKey]) constraint.

testCases.title: Re-scan refreshes title/severity but preserves the recipient's readAt
testCases.preconditions: A materialized lead notification that recipient U has already marked read; the underlying alert's severity later changes (e.g. escalates to overdue).
testCases.steps:
1. U marks the notification read.
2. Underlying alert updates and bridge re-runs.
3. U lists notifications.
testCases.expectedResult: The upsert 'update' branch sets only title/severity/body/metadata — it does not touch readAt/archivedAt, so the row stays read while its severity/title reflect the latest state.

testCases.title: Lead alert materializes to the assignee plus admin-routed recipients (union, deduped)
testCases.preconditions: A LeadOperationalAlert with recipientUserId=assignee A; a routing rule routes that eventType to user A as well and to user B.
testCases.steps:
1. Run syncLeadAlertNotifications.
2. List notifications as A and as B.
testCases.testData: assignee A also in a routing rule; plus user B in rule
testCases.expectedResult: A receives exactly one notification (Set dedupes the overlap between entity default and rule), B receives one. Recipients = entity default ∪ resolveRuleRecipients, with no duplicate per user.

testCases.title: Alert with no entity recipient and no matching routing rule materializes nothing
testCases.preconditions: A LeadOperationalAlert with recipientUserId null and no routing rule for its eventType.
testCases.steps: 1. Run syncLeadAlertNotifications.
testCases.expectedResult: recipients set is empty → the alert is skipped (continue); zero UserNotification rows created. No crash.

testCases.title: Only alerts within the 30-day lookback window are materialized
testCases.preconditions: One lead alert created 10 days ago and one created 40 days ago, both with recipient A.
testCases.steps:
1. Run syncLeadAlertNotifications.
2. List A's notifications.
testCases.testData: alert ages: 10d (in window) and 40d (out of window)
testCases.expectedResult: Only the 10-day-old alert is materialized (where createdAt >= now-30d). The 40-day-old alert is excluded, keeping re-runs cheap.

testCases.title: CIS-received fires once per lead to assignee + RD + routed recipients
testCases.preconditions: A lead with cisSubmittedAt set within the lookback, assignedTmUserId and assignedRdUserId populated.
testCases.steps:
1. Run syncLeadCisReceivedNotifications.
2. List notifications as the TM and as the RD.
testCases.expectedResult: TM and RD each get a 'CIS received — <company>' notification (category lead, eventType cis_received, severity warning, body present, deep-link to lead). dedupeKey 'lead-cis-received:<leadId>' fires once per lead; a re-run does not duplicate.

testCases.title: Account with no engagement >90 days notifies owning TM + RD; re-engagement resets the episode
testCases.preconditions: An active account with assignedTmUserId, lastEngagementAt 100 days ago (or null).
testCases.steps:
1. Run syncAccountInactivityNotifications.
2. List TM notifications.
3. Log an engagement (update lastEngagementAt to now), let it go stale again, re-run.
testCases.testData: lastEngagementAt = 100d ago, then re-engaged, then stale
testCases.expectedResult: Step 1 → TM (and RD) get a 'No recent contact — <account>' warning. dedupeKey embeds lastEngagementAt episode, so a continuously-stale account is notified once; after re-engagement-then-stale a NEW notification is produced (fresh episode key).

testCases.title: Every materialized notification carries a resolvable deepLinkType + deepLinkId
testCases.preconditions: Lead, consignment, CIS and account-inactivity notifications materialized.
testCases.steps: 1. GET /api/v1/notifications and inspect each item's deepLink fields.
testCases.expectedResult: Lead/CIS items → deepLinkType 'lead' + the leadId; consignment items → 'consignment' + siteId; account items → 'account' + accountId. The web Notification Center renders these as clickable deep links into the record.

testCases.title: Web header bell shows unread badge count and opens the dropdown feed
testCases.preconditions: Signed-in web session with >0 unread notifications.
testCases.steps:
1. Load the CRM web app.
2. Observe the header bell badge.
3. Click the bell.
testCases.expectedResult: Bell shows an unread count badge (from /unread-count); clicking opens a dropdown listing recent notifications with deep links; opening/marking read updates the badge. (NotificationBell component.)

testCases.title: /notifications page supports All / Unread / Archived tabs, category filters and pagination
testCases.preconditions: Signed-in web session with a varied inbox.
testCases.steps:
1. Navigate to /notifications.
2. Switch among All/Unread/Archived tabs and apply a category filter.
3. Page through results.
testCases.expectedResult: Each tab maps to the correct status filter, the category filter narrows the list, mark-read/mark-all-read/archive controls work, and pagination advances — all reflecting the backing API.

testCases.title: Title with unicode/special characters from company name renders without corruption
testCases.preconditions: A lead whose companyName contains unicode/emoji/quotes (e.g. "Café & Sön's <Pumps> 🚿").
testCases.steps:
1. Run the bridge to materialize the alert.
2. GET /api/v1/notifications and inspect the title.
testCases.expectedResult: Title is stored and returned verbatim (e.g. 'Routing broadcast — Café & Sön's <Pumps> 🚿') with no truncation or encoding corruption; no SQL/JSON injection effect (parameterized via Prisma).

testCases.title: Recipient email format is validated before dispatch using the ReportSchedule regex
testCases.preconditions: Email channel dispatch path (shared sender) invoked with recipient addresses.
testCases.steps:
1. Provide a payload with a malformed recipient email (e.g. 'not-an-email').
2. Attempt dispatch.
testCases.expectedResult: The malformed address is rejected/skipped at the boundary (reuse of the ReportSchedule recipient-email regex) before any send is attempted. NOTE: the in-app inbox itself has no email field; this FR is partial and only exercisable on the email path (see NOT-TC-050).

testCases.title: Email delivery records a PREVIEW attempt and sends nothing until Graph creds land
testCases.preconditions: PARKED — depends on Microsoft Graph credentials (tenantId/clientId/clientSecret/fromUser). Delivery mode config-gated to PREVIEW.
testCases.steps:
1. Trigger an email-eligible event (lead alert / consignment / website-lead / report digest).
2. Inspect the delivery attempt record and the mailbox.
testCases.expectedResult: A delivery attempt row is recorded as PREVIEW and NO email is actually sent. Once Graph creds are provisioned and mode promoted to MICROSOFT_GRAPH, the same path sends a real email via one shared sender.

testCases.title: TM mobile push with deep-link payload for a newly assigned lead
testCases.preconditions: PARKED — no push provider integrated (no expo-notifications/FCM/APNs); depends on provider decision and device-token capture.
testCases.steps:
1. Assign a new lead/customer to a TM.
2. Expect a concise push carrying a deepLinkRef into the record.
testCases.expectedResult: When built: TM receives a concise mobile push deep-linking into the assigned record. Currently no push is delivered (no provider). Test deferred until FR-NOTIF-010 lands.

testCases.title: Past-due (yellow) and credit-hold (red) notifications fan out to account users when the ERP flag toggles
testCases.preconditions: PARKED — depends on Acumatica AR / credit-hold data feed. Severity + routing framework is built; only the scanner/mirror is missing.
testCases.steps:
1. Toggle the Acumatica past-due / credit-hold flag on an account.
2. Expect notifications to TM, RD, Finance (+ dealer) per routing, severity yellow/red; credit-hold gates ordering.
testCases.testData: Acumatica credit-hold = true (mocked when feed available)
testCases.expectedResult: When unblocked: a WARNING (past-due) or CRITICAL (credit-hold) notification fans out to all users on the account plus routed roles, deep-linked to the account; credit-hold blocks portal ordering. Currently no trigger exists — parked on Acumatica.

testCases.title: Generalized quiet-hours suppresses non-critical outbound channels in-window but still records in-app
testCases.preconditions: NOT-BUILT (GAP-N4) — lead-only quiet-hours exists; all-category generalization not yet implemented. Quiet window default 18:00–08:00 PT.
testCases.steps:
1. Within the quiet window, trigger a non-critical event for a user.
2. Inspect outbound channels vs the in-app inbox.
testCases.expectedResult: When built: outbound push/email for non-critical categories is suppressed during the window while the in-app row is still recorded; critical events (per policy) may bypass. Currently only the lead scanner honors quiet-hours — the reusable all-category capability is not built.

testCases.title: Low-urgency events roll into a daily digest instead of a per-event storm
testCases.preconditions: NOT-BUILT — realtime-vs-digest engine not yet implemented (GAP-N3). Intended to reuse the ReportSchedule scan-worker pattern.
testCases.steps:
1. Generate many low-urgency events for a user in a day.
2. Expect a single daily digest entry rather than N individual notifications.
testCases.expectedResult: When built: the 30 events collapse into one daily digest (in-app first; email attaches when Graph lands), fixing the 'order-storm / 30 emails' problem. Currently each event materializes individually — no digest batching.

testCases.title: Routine notifications expire via TTL while audit/PO/credit items are retained permanently
testCases.preconditions: NOT-BUILT — no retention/TTL policy implemented.
testCases.steps:
1. Age routine and compliance notifications past the intended TTL.
2. Inspect which remain.
testCases.expectedResult: When built: routine items are archived/purged after TTL; audit/PO/credit-event notifications are retained as a permanent immutable compliance record. Currently no TTL or retention enforcement exists.

testCases.title: Single event dispatches to multiple channels with per-channel delivery status and retry/backoff
testCases.preconditions: PARTIAL — channel-agnostic in-app dispatcher and idempotent materialization exist; multi-channel fan-out (push/sms) and an all-category observability dashboard are not built (push/sms parked).
testCases.steps:
1. Configure a category for in_app + email + push.
2. Trigger an event and inspect per-channel delivery records.
testCases.expectedResult: in-app delivery succeeds and is observable today; email is PREVIEW-recorded (parked on Graph); push has no provider (parked). When fully built, each channel records status with retry+backoff and dead-letter visibility surfaced in an admin health dashboard across all categories/channels.

testCases.title: Concurrent bridge runs for the same alert do not create duplicate rows
testCases.preconditions: Same source alert; two bridge invocations executed concurrently for the same recipient+dedupeKey.
testCases.steps: 1. Invoke syncLeadAlertNotifications twice in parallel against the same alert.
testCases.testData: Two concurrent sync calls, identical (recipientUserId, dedupeKey)
testCases.expectedResult: At most one row exists for (recipientUserId, dedupeKey) — the @@unique constraint plus upsert semantics prevent duplicates under a race; the loser updates rather than inserting. No unhandled unique-violation surfaces to the caller.

testCases.title: Dealer card-declined / ACH-failed / free-shipping nudge surfaces with admin-editable copy
testCases.preconditions: NOT-BUILT — dealer-facing payment self-service surface and free-shipping nudge not implemented; depends on dealer portal + Acumatica AR (GAP-N9).
testCases.steps:
1. Simulate a declined card / failed ACH / approaching free-shipping threshold for a dealer.
2. Expect a friendly, admin-editable dealer-facing notification.
testCases.testData: card declined; ACH failed; cart $2,750 of $3,000
testCases.expectedResult: When built: dealer sees friendly, admin-authored action copy (update card / retry payment / 'add $250 for free shipping'); internal roles also notified for payment events. Currently no dealer-facing notification surface exists.

testCases.title: Active local user logs in with valid email and password
testCases.preconditions: An ACTIVE user exists with a LOCAL identity (loginEmail = jane.tm@dynamicaqs.com) and a known password set via scrypt hash.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with the valid email and password.
2. Inspect the HTTP status and response body.
3. Decode/inspect tokens, identity, and session fields.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 OK. Response contains identity (userId, role, displayName, email, actorType=internal), session (sessionId, role, issuedAt, expiresAt, refreshExpiresAt, scopes), and tokens (accessToken + refreshToken, with accessTokenExpiresAt ~15 min and refreshTokenExpiresAt ~14 days). user.lastLoginAt is updated and a LOGIN AuditEntry is written.

testCases.title: Email is normalized (trim + lowercase) before identity lookup
testCases.preconditions: An ACTIVE local user exists with stored loginEmail = jane.tm@dynamicaqs.com.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with mixed-case and padded email.
2. Observe whether login succeeds.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 OK and a session is issued; the email is trimmed and lowercased before lookup so it matches the stored loginEmail.

testCases.title: Login with missing email or password is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Auth endpoint reachable.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with empty/absent password.
2. Repeat with empty/absent email.
3. Observe status and message.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized with message 'Email and password are required'. No session issued.

testCases.title: Wrong password is rejected with a generic, non-enumerating error
testCases.preconditions: An ACTIVE local user exists (jane.tm@dynamicaqs.com).
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with the correct email and an incorrect password.
2. Observe status and message text.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized with the generic message 'Invalid email or password' (does NOT reveal whether the email exists). An AUTH_ATTEMPT AuditEntry with result 'rejected_invalid_credentials' is recorded.

testCases.title: Login for an unknown email returns the same generic error (no user enumeration)
testCases.preconditions: No user exists with email ghost@dynamicaqs.com.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with a non-existent email.
2. Compare status/message to the wrong-password case (AUTH-TC-004).
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized with identical generic message 'Invalid email or password' — indistinguishable from a wrong-password response, preventing account enumeration.

testCases.title: Deactivated user is blocked from signing in
testCases.preconditions: A local user exists with correct credentials but isActive = false (deactivated, history preserved).
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with that user's correct email and password.
2. Observe status and message.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized with message 'User is inactive'. No session issued. An AUTH_ATTEMPT AuditEntry with result 'rejected_inactive_user' (carrying the userId) is recorded; the user's historical records remain intact.

testCases.title: Entra-only (non-LOCAL) account cannot log in via password endpoint
testCases.preconditions: A user exists that has only a MICROSOFT_ENTRA identity (no LOCAL identity / no passwordHash).
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with that user's email and any password.
2. Observe response.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized 'Invalid email or password' — the LOCAL-provider lookup finds no identity with a passwordHash, so password login is refused (must use Entra SSO).

testCases.title: Password verification uses scrypt + timing-safe comparison; hash never returned
testCases.preconditions: A local user with a stored hash of the form scrypt$<salt>$<derived> exists.
testCases.steps:
1. Log in successfully (AUTH-TC-001).
2. Inspect the login response payload and server logs.
3. Confirm stored hash format in the DB.
testCases.expectedResult: Password hash is scrypt (salt + 64-byte derived key) compared with timingSafeEqual; plain-text password and the hash are never present in the response body or in any log output.

testCases.title: Auth endpoints reject non-permitted HTTP methods
testCases.preconditions: API running.
testCases.steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/auth/login.
2. Send GET /api/v1/auth/logout (expects POST).
3. Send POST /api/v1/auth/me (expects GET).
testCases.expectedResult: 405 Method Not Allowed for each, with an Allow header naming the permitted method(s) (POST for login/logout, GET for me).

testCases.title: GET /auth/me returns identity and session for a valid access token
testCases.preconditions: A user has an active session and a valid (non-expired, non-revoked) access token.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/auth/me with header Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>.
2. Inspect response.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 OK with { identity, session }. identity reflects current user role/email/actorType; session has correct sessionId, expiresAt, refreshExpiresAt and module scopes for the role.

testCases.title: GET /auth/me without a bearer token returns 401
testCases.preconditions: API running.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/auth/me with no Authorization header.
2. Repeat with a malformed header 'Token abc' and with 'Bearer ' (empty token).
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized with message 'Missing bearer token' for each — readBearerToken only accepts a 'Bearer <token>' scheme with a non-empty token.

testCases.title: Access token of a revoked session is rejected
testCases.preconditions: A session was issued then revoked (logout, password reset, or admin reset).
testCases.steps:
1. Revoke the session.
2. GET /api/v1/auth/me with the now-revoked access token.
testCases.testData: Authorization: Bearer <access token of revoked session>
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized 'Session has been revoked' (surfaced as Invalid session at the route). No identity returned.

testCases.title: Expired access token is rejected at the access-token boundary
testCases.preconditions: A session exists whose expiresAt is in the past (access TTL ~15 min elapsed) but whose refresh token is still valid.
testCases.steps:
1. Advance time past the access expiresAt.
2. GET /api/v1/auth/me with the expired access token.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized — validateActiveSession throws 'Session access token has expired'; /me returns Invalid session.

testCases.title: Session of a user deactivated mid-session is rejected on next request
testCases.preconditions: A user has an active, non-expired session; the admin then sets isActive = false.
testCases.steps:
1. Confirm /auth/me works while active.
2. Deactivate the user via admin.
3. GET /api/v1/auth/me again with the same valid access token.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized 'User is inactive' — validateActiveSession re-checks user.isActive on every token validation, so deactivation takes effect immediately without waiting for token expiry.

testCases.title: Valid refresh token rotates the session and issues new access + refresh tokens
testCases.preconditions: A session exists with a valid, non-expired refresh token.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with the refresh token.
2. Inspect new tokens.
3. Attempt to reuse the OLD refresh token a second time.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 OK with a brand-new accessToken and refreshToken (rotation), updated expiry timestamps, lastSeenAt bumped, and an UPDATE 'refresh' AuditEntry. Rotation happens inside a transaction; the old refresh token no longer resolves to the session.

testCases.title: Refresh with missing/blank/unknown refresh token is rejected
testCases.preconditions: API running.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with no refreshToken.
2. POST with a blank string.
3. POST with a syntactically valid but non-existent token.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized. Missing/blank → 'refreshToken is required'; unknown token → 'Invalid session'. No tokens issued.

testCases.title: Refresh is rejected once the refresh token has expired
testCases.preconditions: A session exists whose refreshExpiresAt is in the past (~14 days elapsed).
testCases.steps:
1. Advance time past refreshExpiresAt.
2. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with that refresh token.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized 'Session refresh token has expired'. No new tokens issued; user must re-authenticate.

testCases.title: Refresh on a revoked session is rejected
testCases.preconditions: A session was revoked (logout or password reset) but its refresh token is still within TTL.
testCases.steps:
1. Revoke the session.
2. POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with the still-in-TTL refresh token.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 Unauthorized 'Session has been revoked' — a revoked session cannot be revived via refresh.

testCases.title: Logout revokes the current session and is idempotent
testCases.preconditions: A user has an active session and valid access token.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/logout with Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>.
2. Inspect response.
3. GET /auth/me with the same token.
4. POST /api/v1/auth/logout again with the same (now-revoked) token.
testCases.expectedResult: First logout: 200 OK { sessionId, revokedAt }; session.revokedReason set to 'logout' and a LOGOUT AuditEntry written. Subsequent /me returns 401. A second logout call does not re-revoke or error beyond returning the session state (only revokes when not already revoked).

testCases.title: Logout rejects an explicit refreshToken in the body (access-token-only contract)
testCases.preconditions: A valid access token exists.
testCases.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/auth/logout with a valid bearer token AND a refreshToken in the body.
testCases.expectedResult: 400 Bad Request 'Logout currently uses bearer access token only'. The session is NOT revoked by this rejected call.

testCases.title: Forgot-password for an eligible active local account prepares a reset (preview enabled)
testCases.preconditions: previewEnabled=true in the environment; an ACTIVE local user with a passwordHash exists.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password with the user's email.
2. Inspect response and DB.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 OK with delivery='preview', a previewResetUrl, previewToken and expiresAt. A PasswordResetToken row is created (tokenHash stored, not raw) and a CREATE PASSWORD_RESET AuditEntry 'forgot_password_requested' is written.

testCases.title: Forgot-password for unknown / non-local / inactive accounts returns a generic suppressed response
testCases.preconditions: Three cases: (a) email belongs to no user, (b) email is Entra-only (no passwordHash), (c) user is inactive.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password for each of (a), (b), (c).
2. Compare responses.
testCases.expectedResult: All return 200 OK with accepted=true, delivery='suppressed' and the same generic message; no reset token is created. The responses are indistinguishable from each other (no enumeration), while a PASSWORD_RESET AuditEntry records the true result internally (suppressed_unknown_or_non_local / suppressed_inactive_user).

testCases.title: Forgot-password returns 'unavailable' when delivery preview is disabled
testCases.preconditions: previewEnabled=false; an eligible active local user exists.
testCases.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password with the eligible user's email.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 OK with accepted=true, delivery='unavailable' and a message instructing to ask an admin to reset the account. No reset token is created; a 'delivery_unavailable' audit entry is recorded.

testCases.title: Requesting a new reset token invalidates the prior unused token for that user
testCases.preconditions: previewEnabled=true; an eligible active local user already has one unused, unexpired reset token.
testCases.steps:
1. POST forgot-password to generate token T1.
2. POST forgot-password again to generate token T2.
3. Attempt reset-password using T1.
testCases.testData: Two sequential forgot-password calls for jane.tm@dynamicaqs.com
testCases.expectedResult: T2 is created and all prior unused tokens (including T1) are marked usedAt in the same transaction. Reset with T1 fails ('Password reset link is invalid or has expired'); only the latest token T2 works.

testCases.title: Forgot-password with missing email is rejected
testCases.preconditions: API running.
testCases.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password with no/blank email.
testCases.expectedResult: 400 Bad Request 'Email is required'.

testCases.title: Valid reset token sets a new password and revokes all of the user's active sessions
testCases.preconditions: previewEnabled=true; a valid unused, unexpired reset token exists for an active local user who also has at least one active session.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password with the token and a compliant new password.
2. Confirm old sessions are revoked.
3. Log in with the new password; confirm the old password fails.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 OK { success: true, email }. The identity passwordHash is re-derived (scrypt), the token is marked usedAt, and ALL of the user's non-revoked sessions are revoked with revokedReason='password_reset' (atomic transaction). Old password no longer works; new password authenticates.

testCases.title: Reset with an invalid / unknown token is rejected
testCases.preconditions: No reset token matches the supplied value.
testCases.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password with a bogus token and a valid new password.
testCases.expectedResult: 400 Bad Request 'Password reset link is invalid or has expired'. A REJECT 'reset_rejected_invalid_token' audit entry is recorded.

testCases.title: Reset with an already-used or expired token is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Two tokens: (a) one already consumed (usedAt set), (b) one whose expiresAt is in the past.
testCases.steps:
1. POST reset-password with the used token.
2. POST reset-password with the expired token.
testCases.expectedResult: Both return 400 'Password reset link is invalid or has expired'. Audit records distinguish 'reset_rejected_used_token' vs 'reset_rejected_expired_token'. Password is not changed.

testCases.title: New password shorter than 10 characters is rejected
testCases.preconditions: A valid unused reset token exists.
testCases.steps:
1. POST reset-password with a 9-character new password.
2. POST again with exactly 10 characters.
testCases.expectedResult: 9-char password → 400 'New password must be at least 10 characters long'. Exactly 10 chars → accepted (boundary inclusive). Missing/blank newPassword → 400 'New password is required'; missing token → 400 'Password reset token is required'.

testCases.title: Reset rejected for non-LOCAL identity or inactive user
testCases.preconditions: Two valid tokens: (a) one tied to a non-LOCAL (Entra) identity, (b) one tied to a user who was deactivated after the token was issued.
testCases.steps:
1. POST reset-password with token (a).
2. POST reset-password with token (b).
testCases.testData: Valid tokens for an Entra-only identity and for a since-deactivated user, with newPassword 'Brand-New-Pass-12'.
testCases.expectedResult: (a) 400 'Password reset is only available for local Pulse accounts' (audit 'reset_rejected_non_local_identity'); (b) 400 'User is inactive' (audit 'reset_rejected_inactive_user'). No password change.

testCases.title: Reset token cannot be replayed after a successful reset (TOCTOU)
testCases.preconditions: A valid unused reset token exists for an active local user.
testCases.steps:
1. POST reset-password with the token and a valid new password (succeeds).
2. Immediately POST reset-password again with the same token and a different new password.
testCases.testData: Same token used twice; passwords 'Brand-New-Pass-12' then 'Attacker-Pass-99'
testCases.expectedResult: First call 200 success; second call 400 'Password reset link is invalid or has expired' because the token was atomically marked usedAt in the first transaction. The second password is never applied.

testCases.title: Start Entra login returns an authorization URL and persists single-use state
testCases.preconditions: Entra is fully configured (tenantId, clientId, clientSecret, redirectUri set; enabled=true).
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/entra/start with an optional nextPath.
2. Inspect the returned authorizationUrl and DB authLoginState row.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 OK with provider='microsoft_entra', an authorizationUrl containing client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope, prompt=select_account and a random state, plus expiresAt (~10 min). An AuthLoginState row stores the SHA-256 state hash (not the raw state) and the normalized nextPath.

testCases.title: Start Entra login is unavailable when Entra is not configured
testCases.preconditions: One or more Entra env values are missing or enabled=false.
testCases.steps: 1. POST /api/v1/auth/entra/start.
testCases.expectedResult: 503 Service Unavailable (MicrosoftEntraAuthUnavailableError) — 'Microsoft Entra auth is not configured'. No state row is created.

testCases.title: Open-redirect protection: unsafe nextPath values are sanitized
testCases.preconditions: Entra configured.
testCases.steps:
1. POST entra/start with nextPath='//evil.com'.
2. POST with nextPath='https://evil.com'.
3. POST with nextPath='/auth/login'.
4. Complete a login and observe the returned nextPath.
testCases.expectedResult: Protocol-relative and absolute URLs are dropped (stored null); any '/auth/...' path is rewritten to '/leads'; only safe same-site paths beginning with a single '/' are retained. No external redirect target is ever honored.

testCases.title: Existing internal user signs in via Entra and a session is issued
testCases.preconditions: Entra configured; a valid unused state exists; the Entra subject already maps to an existing ACTIVE INTERNAL user, OR a group-role mapping resolves an internal role.
testCases.steps:
1. Drive the OAuth callback to POST /api/v1/auth/entra/complete with the code and state.
2. Inspect the issued session and identity.
testCases.expectedResult: 200 OK with identity (actorType=internal), session, and tokens. The Entra identity is upserted/linked, lastLoginAt updated, the authLoginState marked usedAt, and a LOGIN AuditEntry recorded. Effective role is the highest-priority mapped internal role.

testCases.title: Complete with missing code or state is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Entra configured.
testCases.steps:
1. POST entra/complete with code but no state.
2. POST with state but no code.
testCases.expectedResult: 400 Bad Request 'Missing Microsoft Entra authorization code or state'. No session issued.

testCases.title: CSRF/state protection: unknown, expired, or already-used state is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Entra configured. Three states: unknown (never issued), expired (>10 min old), and already-consumed (usedAt set).
testCases.steps:
1. POST entra/complete with a code and an unknown state.
2. Repeat with an expired state.
3. Repeat by replaying a state already used in a prior successful login.
testCases.expectedResult: Unknown/wrong-provider state → 401 'authorization state was not recognized'; expired or already-used state → 401 'authorization state expired'. State is single-use (marked usedAt on success), preventing replay.

testCases.title: A dealer / non-internal user is denied internal workspace access via Entra
testCases.preconditions: Entra configured; the resolved email/subject links to a user whose userType != INTERNAL (e.g. DEALER).
testCases.steps: 1. Drive entra/complete for a dealer-linked account.
testCases.testData: Entra identity resolving to a DEALER user
testCases.expectedResult: 403 Forbidden 'This Microsoft account is not allowed to access the internal Pulse workspace'. A 'rejected_non_internal_user' auth_attempt audit entry is recorded; no internal session is issued.

testCases.title: Domain allow-list is fail-closed: new identity from a non-approved (or any, when list empty) domain is denied
testCases.preconditions: Entra configured. Case A: allowedDomains=[] (empty). Case B: allowedDomains=['dynamicaqs.com'] and the new user's email is @contractor.io.
testCases.steps:
1. For a NEW Entra identity (no existing UserIdentity), drive entra/complete under Case A.
2. Repeat under Case B with a non-listed domain.
testCases.testData: New identity email new.user@contractor.io under empty allowlist, then under ['dynamicaqs.com']
testCases.expectedResult: 403 Forbidden 'This Microsoft account email domain is not approved for internal Pulse access' in both cases — an empty allowlist DENIES all new identities (fail-closed), and a populated allowlist denies domains not on it. A 'rejected_domain_not_allowed' audit entry is recorded.

testCases.title: Email-linking disabled blocks linking an Entra login to an existing email-matched user with no group mapping
testCases.preconditions: Entra configured; policy.allowEmailLinking=false; an existing user shares the Entra email but the subject has no prior identity and no group-role mapping resolves.
testCases.steps: 1. Drive entra/complete for that email with no mapped role.
testCases.testData: Existing user jane.tm@dynamicaqs.com, new Entra subject, allowEmailLinking=false, no group mapping
testCases.expectedResult: 403 Forbidden 'Email-based Microsoft account linking is disabled...'. Audit 'rejected_email_linking_disabled'. No identity linked.

testCases.title: Auto-provisioning disabled blocks creating a brand-new user even when a group-role maps
testCases.preconditions: Entra configured; policy.autoProvisionFromGroups=false; no existing user/identity matches; a group-role mapping resolves an internal role; domain is allowed.
testCases.steps: 1. Drive entra/complete for a fully-new internal-mapped user.
testCases.testData: New email new.exec@dynamicaqs.com mapped via group to EXECUTIVE, autoProvisionFromGroups=false
testCases.expectedResult: 403 Forbidden 'Automatic Microsoft account provisioning is disabled...'. Audit 'rejected_auto_provision_disabled'. No user created.

testCases.title: No approved Pulse role resolved → access denied
testCases.preconditions: Entra configured; domain allowed; no group-role mapping matches the user's groups and there is no linked user role to inherit.
testCases.steps: 1. Drive entra/complete for a domain-allowed user whose groups map to nothing.
testCases.testData: Allowed-domain new user with non-matching Entra group ids
testCases.expectedResult: 403 Forbidden 'No approved Pulse role was resolved for this Microsoft account'. Audit 'rejected_no_mapped_role'. No session issued.

testCases.title: Highest-priority internal role wins when a user maps to multiple groups; stored mapping overrides env
testCases.preconditions: Entra configured; the user's groups map to two roles (e.g. SALES_BD_REP and EXECUTIVE) and one group exists in both env-var map and admin-stored map with different roles.
testCases.steps:
1. Configure overlapping group-role mappings.
2. Drive entra/complete and inspect the resolved role.
testCases.testData: Groups mapping to {SALES_BD_REP(50), EXECUTIVE(90)}; a group present in both env and stored maps
testCases.expectedResult: The resolved role is the highest-priority internal role (EXECUTIVE here). For the duplicated group, the admin-stored mapping overrides the env-var entry. DEALER_PORTAL_USER is never selectable as an internal role.

testCases.title: Global-scope roles see all records (no scope filter applied)
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated actors for each global role: SUPER_ADMIN, EXECUTIVE, SALES_BD_REP, SALES_BD_LEADERSHIP, FINANCE, ADMIN_CSR_OPS, TRAINING_OPS.
testCases.steps:
1. For each global role, resolve the lead/account/territory record scope.
2. Query the lead/account list.
testCases.testData: Actor role = each of the seven global-scope roles
testCases.expectedResult: buildLeadRecordScope / buildAccountRecordScope return undefined (no WHERE filter) for all seven roles, so each sees the complete record set across all territories/regions.

testCases.title: Territory Manager sees only their own book (owned + managed territory)
testCases.preconditions: A TM actor; some leads/accounts are assigned to the TM (assignedTmUserId) or in a territory they manage (managerUserId); others belong to a different TM.
testCases.steps:
1. As the TM, list leads and accounts.
2. Verify the returned set.
testCases.testData: TM userId = U-TM-1; mix of own and other-TM leads/accounts
testCases.expectedResult: Only records where assignedTmUserId = U-TM-1 OR the territory's managerUserId = U-TM-1 are returned; records owned by other TMs are excluded. Lead visibility additionally respects the pre-handoff gate (see AUTH-TC-047).

testCases.title: Regional Director sees only their region (directed region + owned/managed records)
testCases.preconditions: An RD actor directing one region; leads/accounts/territories exist inside and outside that region.
testCases.steps:
1. As the RD, list leads, accounts, and territories.
2. Verify scope boundaries.
testCases.testData: RD userId = U-RD-1 directing Region R1; records in R1 and in R2
testCases.expectedResult: Only records where assignedRdUserId = U-RD-1 OR the territory's region.directorUserId = U-RD-1 are returned. Records in regions the RD does not direct are excluded.

testCases.title: TM pre-handoff lead gate hides not-yet-handed-off leads unless policy enables pre-handoff visibility
testCases.preconditions: A TM owns leads that are NOT CUSTOMER_ACTIVE and NOT MANUAL_OVERRIDE. TerritoryPolicy 'default' preHandoffTmVisibility toggled between false and true.
testCases.steps:
1. With preHandoffTmVisibility=false, list the TM's leads.
2. Set preHandoffTmVisibility=true and re-list.
testCases.testData: TM with a lead in a pre-handoff stage; territoryPolicy.default.preHandoffTmVisibility=false then true
