testCases.expectedResult: With the flag false, the TM only sees their leads that are CUSTOMER_ACTIVE or MANUAL_OVERRIDE; pre-handoff leads are hidden. With the flag true, the gate is removed and the TM sees all of their owned/managed leads regardless of stage.

testCases.title: Unknown / unmapped role gets a deny-all record scope sentinel
testCases.preconditions: An actor whose role is neither a global-scope role, TM, nor RD reaches a record-scope build.
testCases.steps:
1. Resolve buildLeadRecordScope / buildAccountRecordScope / buildTerritoryRecordScope for such an actor.
2. Run a query with that scope.
testCases.testData: Actor with a residual/unmapped role (e.g. DEALER_PORTAL_USER reaching an internal record query)
testCases.expectedResult: The scope returns the sentinel { id: '__no-record-scope__' } / SQL FALSE, which matches no rows — default-deny ensures no internal records leak to an unscoped role.

testCases.title: Prisma record scope and raw-SQL mirror stay in lockstep
testCases.preconditions: Same TM/RD actor and the same dataset accessed through both the Prisma where path and the raw-SQL aggregation path (e.g. dashboard stage-aging rollup).
testCases.steps:
1. List leads via the Prisma scope.
2. Run the raw-SQL aggregation that uses buildLeadRecordScopeSql.
3. Compare the row sets.
testCases.testData: TM and RD actors over a fixed lead dataset
testCases.expectedResult: The set of leads visible via the Prisma path exactly equals the set counted by the SQL mirror (parity guaranteed by the record-scope-sql regression test), including the pre-handoff gate behavior.

testCases.title: Dealer-portal user is isolated to their own company and cannot reach internal/other-company records (IDOR)
testCases.preconditions: An authenticated DEALER_PORTAL_USER bounded to Company A; records exist for Company B and internal leads.
testCases.steps:
1. As the dealer, request a resource id belonging to Company B (direct id in the path/body).
2. Attempt to list internal leads/accounts.
testCases.testData: Dealer of Company A requesting Company B order id and internal lead ids
testCases.expectedResult: Access is denied / record not found — isolation is resolved server-side from actor.userId (not from a request parameter), so swapping ids never exposes another company's or internal data. No cross-account visibility at any point.

testCases.title: Default-deny module/action gates block a role lacking the required permission
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated actors of several roles; a protected endpoint requires a specific module + action (e.g. admin.integration_manage).
testCases.steps:
1. Call the protected endpoint as a role WITHOUT the action (e.g. TERRITORY_MANAGER calling admin integration management).
2. Call it as a role WITH the action (e.g. SUPER_ADMIN).
3. Call with an unknown/garbage role.
testCases.testData: Endpoint requiring admin.integration_manage; actors TERRITORY_MANAGER, SUPER_ADMIN, and an unknown role
testCases.expectedResult: Roles without the action get 403 Forbidden (server-side, not just UI-hidden); unknown role/module/action is rejected by allowlist .includes default-deny; only the permitted role (SUPER_ADMIN) succeeds. The denial path is enforced even if the UI tab were bypassed.

testCases.title: Authorization denials and auth events are written to an immutable audit trail
testCases.preconditions: An authenticated actor; a protected endpoint they lack permission for.
testCases.steps:
1. Trigger an authorization denial against a protected endpoint.
2. Inspect the AuditEntry created.
3. Attempt to update or delete that audit entry via any API.
testCases.testData: TM hitting an admin-only endpoint; then attempt PATCH/DELETE on the audit entry
testCases.expectedResult: A REJECT AuditEntry of entityType AUTHORIZATION_ATTEMPT is recorded with actorUserId, actorRole, module, actionKey, method, path, ipAddress, userAgent and message. Audit entries are create-only — no update/delete endpoint exists, so the trail is immutable. An audit failure never crashes the request.

testCases.title: Session tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes; raw tokens never persisted
testCases.preconditions: A user logs in successfully, creating a Session row.
testCases.steps:
1. Log in to create a session.
2. Inspect the Session, PasswordResetToken, and AuthLoginState rows in the DB.
testCases.testData: Session created by a normal password login
testCases.expectedResult: accessTokenHash / refreshTokenHash store SHA-256 digests (not the raw opaque tokens); reset tokens store tokenHash; Entra login state stores stateHash. The raw access/refresh/reset/state values exist only in responses to the client, never at rest.

testCases.title: No raw payment-card data is ever accepted or stored by the auth/session or any layer
testCases.preconditions: API running; PCI hard-block in force (card-on-file capture descoped).
testCases.steps:
1. Attempt to submit a raw PAN/CVV anywhere a payment reference is captured (e.g. CIS/payment integration path).
2. Confirm only tokenized/masked references are retained.
testCases.expectedResult: Raw card data is rejected / never persisted; only tokenized or masked references are stored. This boundary holds at every layer (NFR-AD-008). Note: live payment-provider runtime is parked; only the no-raw-card invariant is asserted here.

testCases.title: Admin updates Entra policy via the governed editor; change is persisted and audited atomically
testCases.preconditions: An admin with admin.integration_manage permission; Entra policy stored in FeatureFlag.
testCases.steps:
1. As an authorized admin, update allowEmailLinking, autoProvisionFromGroups, allowedDomains, and groupRoleMappings (structured group + role select).
2. Re-read the resolved policy.
3. Inspect the audit trail.
testCases.testData: { allowEmailLinking: true, allowedDomains: ['Dynamicaqs.com',' DynamicAQS.com '], groupRoleMappings: [{ groupId: 'G-123', role: 'FINANCE' }] }
testCases.expectedResult: Policy upserts into the FeatureFlag with state ON; domains are normalized (trim+lowercase+dedupe → ['dynamicaqs.com']); invalid/blank group or role entries are dropped and roles normalized; an UPDATE AuditEntry (entityType microsoft_entra_policy) is written in the SAME transaction as the flag write.

testCases.title: Non-admin role cannot read or mutate Entra integration policy
testCases.preconditions: Authenticated actors of non-admin roles (e.g. TERRITORY_MANAGER, SALES_BD_REP).
testCases.steps:
1. As a non-admin, call the Entra integration settings GET (requires admin.integration_view).
2. As a non-admin, call the update endpoint (requires admin.integration_manage).
testCases.testData: TERRITORY_MANAGER and SALES_BD_REP actors against Entra settings GET/PATCH
testCases.expectedResult: 403 Forbidden on both read and write — view requires admin.integration_view and mutation requires admin.integration_manage; default-deny applies. A REJECT audit entry is recorded for the denied attempt.

testCases.title: Partial policy update preserves unspecified fields
testCases.preconditions: An existing stored Entra policy with non-default values for all fields.
testCases.steps:
1. Submit an update setting ONLY allowEmailLinking, omitting allowedDomains and groupRoleMappings.
2. Re-read the policy.
testCases.expectedResult: Only allowEmailLinking changes; allowedDomains and groupRoleMappings retain their prior stored values (each field falls back to current when undefined). No fields are silently reset to defaults.

testCases.title: Login input tolerates special characters / unicode and very long passwords without injection
testCases.preconditions: A local user exists; test crafted inputs do not match any real credential.
testCases.steps:
1. POST login with a SQL-injection-style email.
2. POST with a unicode email and an emoji-laden password.
3. POST with a 5,000-character password string.
testCases.testData: email: "' OR 1=1;-- @x.com"; email: "tëst@dynamicaqs.com", password: "pâss🔐word"; a 5000-char password
testCases.expectedResult: All return 401 'Invalid email or password' with no server error, no SQL injection (Prisma parameterizes), and no crash on large inputs. Email normalization (trim/lowercase) is applied; nothing is leaked.

testCases.title: Concurrent refresh attempts with the same token do not yield two live token pairs
testCases.preconditions: A session with a valid refresh token; two requests fire the same refresh token near-simultaneously.
testCases.steps:
1. Issue two parallel POST /api/v1/auth/refresh calls with the identical refresh token.
2. Inspect which tokens remain valid afterward.
testCases.testData: Two concurrent refresh requests, same refreshToken
testCases.expectedResult: Rotation occurs inside a DB transaction keyed on the session; the token hash is replaced, so at most one rotation result remains usable. The superseded refresh token no longer resolves to the session (no two divergent live sessions from one token).

testCases.title: Bootstrap admin seed creates a single usable LOCAL admin idempotently
testCases.preconditions: BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN email/password configured; login or forgot-password triggers ensureBootstrapAdminSeeded.
testCases.steps:
1. Trigger seeding twice (e.g. two logins) concurrently.
2. Inspect the user/identity rows for the bootstrap email.
testCases.testData: Bootstrap admin email admin@dynamicaqs.com configured with a password and role
testCases.expectedResult: Exactly one INTERNAL active user and one LOCAL identity exist for the bootstrap email (upsert is idempotent and the seed promise is de-duplicated); the admin can authenticate with the configured password. If email or password is unset, no seed occurs.

testCases.title: Audit date-range filter (parked) over auth events
testCases.preconditions: Multiple auth/session audit entries exist across a date span. NOTE: date-range filtering is NOT built (FR-AD-049 / FR-AD-046).
testCases.steps:
1. Open the audit monitor.
2. Apply a date-range filter (e.g. last 7 days) over LOGIN/LOGOUT/REJECT entries.
3. Verify only in-range entries return.
testCases.testData: from=2026-06-22, to=2026-06-29 over auth audit entries
testCases.expectedResult: When built: only audit entries within the range are returned. Currently the date-range filter is Not-built (only actor/action/entity-type filters exist), so this case is expected to fail until the filter is implemented.

testCases.title: Unauthenticated request to an admin endpoint is rejected with 401
testCases.preconditions: API running; no Authorization header supplied.
testCases.steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/admin/users with NO Authorization header.
2. Observe the HTTP status and body.
testCases.expectedResult: Response is 401 Unauthorized with message 'Missing bearer token'; no user data is returned.

testCases.title: Request with an invalid/garbage bearer token is rejected with 401
testCases.preconditions: API running.
testCases.steps:
1. Send GET /api/v1/admin/users with Authorization: Bearer not-a-real-token.
2. Observe the response.
testCases.expectedResult: Response is 401 Unauthorized with message 'Invalid session'; the token resolves to no actor.

testCases.title: Token belonging to a revoked or expired session is rejected
testCases.preconditions: A valid session exists for an internal user, then is revoked (e.g. via logout) or its access TTL (15 min) has elapsed.
testCases.steps:
1. Authenticate and capture a valid access token.
2. Revoke the session (POST /api/v1/auth/logout) OR wait past the access-token expiry.
3. Call GET /api/v1/auth/me with the now-stale token.
testCases.testData: Access token from a logged-out / expired session
testCases.expectedResult: Response is 401; validateActiveSession throws 'Session has been revoked' (revoked) or 'Session access token has expired' (expired). No session state returned.

testCases.title: Active session of a user deactivated mid-session is rejected on next request
testCases.preconditions: User U has a live, non-expired session; an admin then deactivates U (isActive=false).
testCases.steps:
1. As U, hold a valid access token.
2. Admin deactivates U.
3. U calls any authenticated endpoint with the token.
testCases.testData: U.isActive flipped to false while token still within TTL
testCases.expectedResult: Request is rejected (401); validateActiveSession throws 'User is inactive'. Deactivation blocks access without deleting U's historical records.

testCases.title: Role without the admin module cannot reach any admin endpoint (server-side)
testCases.preconditions: Valid sessions exist for SALES_BD_REP, TERRITORY_MANAGER, REGIONAL_DIRECTOR, TRAINING_OPS (none have the 'admin' module in ROLE_DEFAULT_MODULE_ACCESS).
testCases.steps:
1. As each role above, send GET /api/v1/admin/users (module gate 'admin').
2. Observe the response per role.
testCases.expectedResult: Each request returns 403 Forbidden (assertModuleAccess throws AuthorizationError 'Role X cannot access module admin'); enforced server-side regardless of UI state.

testCases.title: Role with admin module but without the specific action is denied that action
testCases.preconditions: FINANCE has the 'admin' module but its action allowlist excludes admin.user_manage and admin.integration_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. As FINANCE, send POST /api/v1/admin/users (requires admin.user_manage).
2. As FINANCE, send a PATCH to an integration settings endpoint (requires admin.integration_manage).
3. Observe each response.
testCases.expectedResult: Both mutating requests return 403 (assertActionAccess throws 'Role FINANCE cannot perform action admin.user_manage' / 'admin.integration_manage'). Action gate is independent of the module gate.

testCases.title: ADMIN_CSR_OPS and SUPER_ADMIN can perform granted admin actions
testCases.preconditions: Valid sessions for ADMIN_CSR_OPS and SUPER_ADMIN; both hold admin.user_manage and admin.integration_manage (SUPER_ADMIN holds all actions except consignment.sync).
testCases.steps:
1. As ADMIN_CSR_OPS, GET /api/v1/admin/users and POST a new user.
2. As SUPER_ADMIN, repeat.
3. Observe responses.
testCases.expectedResult: Both roles successfully list (200) and create (2xx) users; actions are permitted by their allowlists.

testCases.title: Global-scope roles see all lead/account records (no scope filter)
testCases.preconditions: Records exist owned by multiple TMs across multiple regions. Actor roles: EXECUTIVE, SUPER_ADMIN, SALES_BD_REP, SALES_BD_LEADERSHIP, FINANCE, ADMIN_CSR_OPS, TRAINING_OPS.
testCases.steps:
1. As each global-scope role, query the leads/accounts list.
2. Compare the returned set to the full record set.
testCases.testData: Seed: 3 TMs each owning leads in different regions
testCases.expectedResult: buildLeadRecordScope/buildAccountRecordScope returns undefined (no WHERE filter); all records are visible to every global-scope role.

testCases.title: TM sees only owned/managed records, not another TM's book (IDOR-resistant list)
testCases.preconditions: TM-A owns/has-territory accounts A1,A2; TM-B owns B1. preHandoffTmVisibility default (false).
testCases.steps:
1. As TM-A, list accounts/leads.
2. Verify the result set.
testCases.testData: TM-A.userId; accounts A1,A2 (assignedTmUserId=A or territory.managerUserId=A), B1 (assignedTmUserId=B)
testCases.expectedResult: Only A1,A2 returned. Scope WHERE filters to assignedTmUserId=actor OR territory.managerUserId=actor; B1 is excluded. For leads, also gated to CUSTOMER_ACTIVE or MANUAL_OVERRIDE when preHandoffTmVisibility=false.

testCases.title: TM directly requesting another TM's record id is denied (no cross-book read)
testCases.preconditions: Lead/account B1 belongs to TM-B; TM-A is authenticated.
testCases.steps:
1. As TM-A, request the record by B1's exact id (e.g. GET /leads/{B1.id}).
2. Observe the result.
testCases.testData: TM-A token; path id = B1.id (not in A's book)
testCases.expectedResult: Record is not returned (404/empty) because the scoped query (findFirst with AND[scope,{id}]) excludes it; the id is not parameter-trusted. Note: per RBAC audit, leads intake mutators currently use unscoped findUnique (LOW, not exploitable — TM lacks lead.intake_manage); read/list paths are scoped.

testCases.title: RD sees records in own region only, not other regions
testCases.preconditions: RD-X directs Region 1; Region 2 has its own director. Records exist in both regions.
testCases.steps:
1. As RD-X, list leads/accounts/territories.
2. Verify region membership of returned records.
testCases.testData: RD-X.userId; records in Region 1 and Region 2
testCases.expectedResult: Only Region 1 records returned (assignedRdUserId=actor OR territory.region.directorUserId=actor). Region 2 records excluded.

testCases.title: A scoped role with no defined scope branch gets a deny-all sentinel
testCases.preconditions: Actor whose role is neither global nor TM nor RD reaches a record-scope builder (e.g. DEALER_PORTAL_USER routed through a scoped builder).
testCases.steps:
1. Invoke buildAccountRecordScope/buildLeadRecordScope with such an actor.
2. Run the resulting query.
testCases.expectedResult: Builder returns { id: '__no-record-scope__' } (SQL mirror returns FALSE); the query matches zero rows — default-deny rather than accidental all-access.

testCases.title: Dealer-portal user is bounded to own company; cannot see another company's data
testCases.preconditions: Dealer user D1 in company C1; data exists for company C2.
testCases.steps:
1. As D1, attempt to read orders/data belonging to C2 (by id and by list).
2. Observe the result.
testCases.testData: D1 (UserKind.DEALER, company C1); C2 order id
testCases.expectedResult: Only C1 context is visible; C2 records are not returned at any point. Isolation is resolved server-side from actor.userId, not from a request parameter.

testCases.title: Dealer user attempting to escalate company by passing another companyId is ignored
testCases.preconditions: Dealer user D1 in company C1.
testCases.steps:
1. As D1, send a request including a body/query parameter companyId=C2.
2. Observe whether C2 scope is honored.
testCases.expectedResult: Parameter is not trusted; the server derives company context from D1's identity. No C2 data is returned (no parameter-trusting cross-tenant access).

testCases.title: Free-text field containing a Luhn-valid PAN is rejected, not stored
testCases.preconditions: assertNoRawPaymentCardData guards persisted free-text fields (CIS note, lead note, public CIS form).
testCases.steps:
1. Submit a CIS/lead note whose text contains a real-structured card number.
2. Observe the result and confirm nothing was persisted/logged.
testCases.expectedResult: Save is rejected with an error ending '...appears to contain payment card data, which cannot be stored in Pulse...'. No PAN is written to any table, log, or audit record.

testCases.title: PAN obfuscated with zero-width / invisible characters is still detected
testCases.preconditions: PCI guard strips INVISIBLE_FORMATTING (U+00AD, U+200B–U+200D, U+FEFF) before matching.
testCases.steps:
1. Submit a note containing a PAN interleaved with zero-width spaces.
2. Observe the result.
testCases.expectedResult: Invisible chars are stripped; the 16-digit Luhn-valid PAN is detected and the save is rejected with the PCI message.

testCases.title: PAN typed into any (non-card-named) field of the public CIS form is refused
testCases.preconditions: assertNoRawPaymentCardDataInRecord scans every string value of the submitted CIS form one level deep.
testCases.steps:
1. Submit the public CIS form with a PAN placed in an unrelated field (e.g. 'comments' or 'businessName').
2. Observe the result.
testCases.expectedResult: Form is rejected with 'This form appears to contain payment card data...'; the form is not persisted regardless of which field held the PAN.

testCases.title: Non-card numeric strings (phone, order id, timestamp) are NOT rejected
testCases.preconditions: Guard requires length 13–19, MII prefix [2–6], and Luhn pass; excludes comma/slash/colon separators.
testCases.steps:
1. Submit notes containing a phone number, a millisecond timestamp, and a comma-separated number list.
2. Confirm each saves successfully.
testCases.expectedResult: All save successfully — timestamps start with 1 (excluded by MII [2-6]); phone/short numbers fail length or Luhn; comma-separated list is not concatenated. No false rejection.

testCases.title: Empty, null, and 12-digit boundary inputs are handled without error
testCases.preconditions: containsLikelyPaymentCardNumber accepts string | null | undefined.
testCases.steps:
1. Call the guard with null, undefined, '' and a 12-digit number.
2. Call with a 13-digit Luhn-valid Amex-prefixed number.
testCases.expectedResult: null/undefined/''/12-digit (below 13 min) return false (no rejection); a valid 13–19 digit MII[2-6] Luhn-pass number returns true (rejection). No exceptions thrown on null/undefined.

testCases.title: Passwords are stored as salted scrypt hashes, never plaintext; temp passwords are random
testCases.preconditions: Admin creates a user / resets a password.
testCases.steps:
1. Admin creates a user with a temp password (or system-generated).
2. Inspect the stored identity.passwordHash and any logs.
testCases.expectedResult: Stored value has format 'scrypt$<16-byte-hex-salt>$<64-byte-derived-hex>'; no plaintext password appears in DB or logs. Generated temp passwords use 9 bytes base64url crypto-random entropy.

testCases.title: Login with wrong password returns a generic, non-enumerating error and is audited
testCases.preconditions: A local user exists.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with the right email and a wrong password.
2. POST with a non-existent email.
3. Compare the two error messages.
testCases.expectedResult: Both return 401 with identical 'Invalid email or password' (no account-existence leak). verifySecret uses timingSafeEqual. A 'rejected_invalid_credentials' LOGIN audit entry is written.

testCases.title: Deactivated user cannot log in even with correct credentials
testCases.preconditions: Local user with correct password but isActive=false.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/login with valid email + correct password for the inactive user.
2. Observe the response.
testCases.expectedResult: 401 'User is inactive'; no session issued. A 'rejected_inactive_user' LOGIN audit entry is recorded.

testCases.title: Password reset revokes all active sessions and is restricted to LOCAL active accounts
testCases.preconditions: Local active user with a valid, unused, unexpired reset token and at least one live session.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password with token + new password (>=10 chars).
2. Attempt to use a previously-issued access token.
3. Try resetting again with the same (now used) token.
testCases.expectedResult: Reset succeeds; all non-revoked sessions get revokedReason='password_reset'; old token now 401s. Reusing the consumed token returns 400 'Password reset link is invalid or has expired'. Hash updated atomically with audit entry.

testCases.title: Reset is rejected for short password, non-local identity, inactive user, or expired token
testCases.preconditions: Reset tokens prepared for each negative scenario.
testCases.steps:
1. Reset with newPassword of 9 chars.
2. Reset against an Entra (non-LOCAL) identity token.
3. Reset for an inactive user.
4. Reset with an expired token.
testCases.testData: 9-char password; non-local token; inactive-user token; expired token
testCases.expectedResult: 1) 400 'New password must be at least 10 characters long'. 2) 400 'Password reset is only available for local Pulse accounts'. 3) 400 'User is inactive'. 4) 400 'invalid or has expired'. Each rejection writes a REJECT audit entry.

testCases.title: Forgot-password returns a uniform suppressed response for unknown/non-local emails
testCases.preconditions: API running.
testCases.steps:
1. POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password for a known local active user.
2. POST for an unknown email and for a non-local (Entra-only) user.
3. Compare responses.
testCases.expectedResult: All return accepted:true with a generic message; the unknown/non-local cases use delivery:'suppressed' and write a 'suppressed_unknown_or_non_local' audit entry — no account-existence disclosure.

testCases.title: Admin updates Entra group→role mapping via governed editor; change is audited atomically
testCases.preconditions: Actor with admin.integration_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. PATCH the Entra integration settings with groupRoleMappings=[{groupId, role:'FINANCE'}].
2. Re-read settings.
3. Inspect the audit trail.
testCases.expectedResult: Mapping is normalized (role aliased to FINANCE), persisted in FeatureFlag 'auth.microsoft_entra.access', and an UPDATE audit entry (entityType 'microsoft_entra_policy') is written in the same transaction. Stored mapping overrides any env mapping for the same groupId (case-insensitive).

testCases.title: Invalid/blank group-role mapping entries are silently dropped, not stored
testCases.preconditions: Actor with admin.integration_manage.
testCases.steps:
1. PATCH groupRoleMappings with entries: blank groupId, blank role, unknown role string, and a duplicate groupId differing only by case.
2. Re-read the stored policy.
testCases.expectedResult: Blank groupId/role and unknown role 'WIZARD' are dropped (normalizeRole throws and entry is skipped); duplicate g3/G3 is deduped case-insensitively keeping the last. Only valid normalized entries persist.

testCases.title: Empty domain allowlist DENIES a brand-new Entra identity (default fail-closed)
testCases.preconditions: Entra policy at defaults: allowedDomains=[], allowEmailLinking=false, autoProvisionFromGroups=false. No existing identity for the inbound subject.
testCases.steps:
1. Complete an Entra login for a new external subject whose email domain is not in any allowlist.
2. Observe the result.
testCases.testData: new Entra subject; email user@external.com; allowedDomains=[]
testCases.expectedResult: 403 'This Microsoft account email domain is not approved for internal Pulse access'; a 'rejected_domain_not_allowed' audit entry is written. New identity is not admitted (hardened default-deny, commit 24136e5).

testCases.title: Email-linking and auto-provisioning are blocked when their toggles are off
testCases.preconditions: Entra policy: allowEmailLinking=false, autoProvisionFromGroups=false; domain allowed.
testCases.steps:
1. Complete Entra login where email matches an existing local user but no group mapping resolves (linking case).
2. Complete Entra login for a brand-new user where a group mapping DOES resolve (provisioning case).
testCases.testData: Case A: email matches existing user, no mappedRole. Case B: new user, mappedRole=FINANCE
testCases.expectedResult: Case A: 403 'Email-based Microsoft account linking is disabled...' ('rejected_email_linking_disabled'). Case B: 403 'Automatic Microsoft account provisioning is disabled...' ('rejected_auto_provision_disabled'). Both audited.

testCases.title: A DEALER/non-internal user cannot authenticate into the internal workspace via Entra
testCases.preconditions: An existing user whose userType is DEALER (not INTERNAL) matches the Entra email/subject.
testCases.steps:
1. Complete an Entra login that resolves to a non-internal user.
2. Observe the result.
testCases.expectedResult: 403 'This Microsoft account is not allowed to access the internal Pulse workspace' ('rejected_non_internal_user'); no internal session is issued.

testCases.title: Entra login with no resolvable approved Pulse role is rejected
testCases.preconditions: Domain allowed; no group mapping resolves and there is no linked user role.
testCases.steps:
1. Complete Entra login where neither a mapped role nor a linked-user role yields an internal role.
2. Observe the result.
testCases.expectedResult: 401-class rejection 'No approved Pulse role was resolved for this Microsoft account' ('rejected_no_mapped_role'); audited; no session issued.

testCases.title: Authorization denial is written to the audit trail with actor, role, path, and reason
testCases.preconditions: A non-admin authenticated user hits a gated admin endpoint.
testCases.steps:
1. As TERRITORY_MANAGER, call GET /api/v1/admin/users (module-denied).
2. Inspect the audit trail.
testCases.expectedResult: A REJECT audit entry (entityType 'AUTHORIZATION_ATTEMPT') is created with actorUserId, actorRole, module/actionKey, method, path, IP, userAgent, and 'access_denied'. Audit failure never crashes the route (wrapped in try/catch).

testCases.title: No API path can edit or delete an audit entry
testCases.preconditions: Audit entries exist; even SUPER_ADMIN is authenticated.
testCases.steps:
1. Enumerate admin routes for any update/delete on audit entries.
2. Attempt PUT/PATCH/DELETE against an audit entry id as SUPER_ADMIN.
testCases.expectedResult: No mutate/delete endpoint exists (entries are created only via prisma.auditEntry.create); attempts return 404/405. Entries are immutable and retained (min 7 years per NFR-AD-016).

testCases.title: Audit monitor filters by actor/entity/action and paginates at max 100/request
testCases.preconditions: Actor with admin.audit_view; >100 audit entries exist across actors and action types.
testCases.steps:
1. GET /api/v1/admin/audit filtered by actor, then by entityType, then by actionType.
2. Request a page size above 100.
testCases.expectedResult: Filtered results return matching entries within 2s (90-day window). Page size is capped server-side at 100 regardless of requested value. (Date-range filter is Not-built — see SEC-TC-035.)

testCases.title: Audit date-range filter is not yet available
testCases.preconditions: Actor with admin.audit_view.
testCases.steps:
1. Attempt to filter audit entries by a fromDate/toDate range.
2. Observe behavior.
testCases.expectedResult: No date-range filtering is applied (FR-AD-049 Not-built); only actor/entity/action filters take effect. Mark as a known gap to verify once the date-range filter ships.

testCases.title: Audit export is permission-gated and returns only the current filtered view
testCases.preconditions: Audit entries exist; one actor has admin.audit_view, another (e.g. SALES_BD_REP) does not.
testCases.steps:
1. As an audit-view role, apply a filter and export CSV.
2. As a role without admin.audit_view, attempt the same.
testCases.expectedResult: Allowed role exports a CSV of the currently visible/filtered entries (UX-AD-012). Denied role receives 403; export is server-side gated, not just UI-hidden.

testCases.title: Integration view vs manage are separately gated (view-only cannot mutate)
testCases.preconditions: Role with admin.integration_view but NOT admin.integration_manage (e.g. EXECUTIVE — read/oversight allowlist).
testCases.steps:
1. As that role, GET the integration overview.
2. As that role, attempt to PATCH integration settings (Entra/Outlook/payment/lead-alert).
testCases.expectedResult: GET integration overview succeeds (200). Any settings mutation returns 403 (requires admin.integration_manage). EXECUTIVE is read/oversight only (narrowed in commit 24136e5).

testCases.title: Payment integration management never accepts or stores raw card data
testCases.preconditions: Actor with admin.integration_manage. Live provider runtime is parked; manual tokenized-capture recording only.
testCases.steps:
1. Set capture mode (manual recording vs provider runtime), default provider, CIS capture flag.
2. Attempt to submit a raw card number through any payment-related field.
testCases.testData: captureMode='manual'; raw PAN in any text field
testCases.expectedResult: Capture-mode/provider/flag settings persist; no field accepts or stores a raw PAN (only tokenized/masked references). Live payment-provider runtime config is Parked pending provider certification — verify boundary only.

testCases.title: Routing-threshold / SLA-timer write endpoints are not yet wired (config not persisted, not audited)
testCases.preconditions: Admin opens routing/SLA configuration UI (panels rendered; read server state).
testCases.steps:
1. As an admin, change a routing basis/threshold or an SLA timer and submit.
2. Check persistence and audit.
testCases.expectedResult: Write does not persist (POST /admin/routing-thresholds and SLA write endpoints Not-built — UX-AD-008); no config-change audit entry is produced (FR-AD-044 Not-built for routing/settings/flags). Treat as a known Partial gap.

testCases.feature: System Settings & Feature Flags Write Path
testCases.title: System-settings and feature-flag write endpoints are not yet available
testCases.preconditions: Admin opens System Settings and Feature Flags panels (rendered).
testCases.steps:
1. Edit company name/logo/timezone/currency and save.
2. Toggle a feature flag.
testCases.expectedResult: Saves do not persist server-side (POST /admin/system-settings and GET/PATCH /admin/feature-flags Not-built — UX-AD-009/010). Note: the Entra policy feature-flag write IS built and audited (distinct path). Verify the gap and re-test when endpoints ship.

testCases.title: Per-user permission overrides are not built (fixed-role model only)
testCases.preconditions: Fixed role catalog (10 roles); OQ-AD-01 decision pending.
testCases.steps:
1. Attempt to grant a single user an action beyond their assigned role's allowlist.
2. Observe the available controls / API.
testCases.testData: Grant 'admin.integration_manage' to a TERRITORY_MANAGER user only
testCases.expectedResult: No mechanism exists; access is tuned solely by assigning a role profile (BR-AD-06). Override capability is Parked pending OQ-AD-01. Document as Not-built.

testCases.title: Acumatica connectivity shows a warning state pending sandbox certification
testCases.preconditions: Acumatica live sync is parked until sandbox/endpoint certification. Actor with admin.integration_view.
testCases.steps:
1. GET the integration overview.
2. Inspect the Acumatica status row.
testCases.expectedResult: Acumatica row shows 'connected' or 'warning — awaiting sandbox certification' with health/last-checked. No live ERP write/sync is attempted. Live sync remains Parked (Section 5.3).

testCases.title: SQL/parameter injection in admin filters and group mappings is neutralized
testCases.preconditions: Actor with appropriate admin permissions; queries use parameterized Prisma.
testCases.steps:
1. Send an audit/user filter value containing a SQL meta-payload.
2. Send a groupRoleMapping groupId with a SQL/script payload.
testCases.expectedResult: No injection executes — Prisma parameterizes values; the payload is treated as a literal string (and trimmed/normalized for mappings). No data leak or schema change; no 500 from unescaped input.

testCases.title: Concurrent role-change and deactivation on the same user do not corrupt state or skip audit
testCases.preconditions: Two admins act on user U at the same time; user mutations run inside a DB transaction with their audit entry.
testCases.steps:
1. Fire a role-change and a deactivate on U near-simultaneously.
2. Inspect U's final state and the audit entries.
testCases.testData: Admin-1: setRole(FINANCE) on U; Admin-2: deactivate(U) — concurrent
testCases.expectedResult: Each mutation is atomic with its AuditEntry (no partial write, no lost audit). Final state is one of the two consistent outcomes; both changes are independently recorded; prior activity authorship is not rewritten (BR-AD-05).

testCases.title: Audit query at the page-size boundary and beyond returns at most 100 entries
testCases.preconditions: More than 100 audit entries exist; actor has admin.audit_view.
testCases.steps:
1. Request pageSize=100.
2. Request pageSize=101.
3. Request pageSize=0 / negative.
testCases.expectedResult: 100 returns up to 100; 101 is clamped to 100; 0/negative fall back to a safe default page (no error, no full-table dump). Server-side cap (max 100) is enforced.
